(On the date specified),—when the mahārājādhirāja rāja-paramêśvara, master of the eastern southern and western oceans, vira-pratāpa Achyuta-Dêva- Rāya-mahārāya was ruling the kingdom of the world :—by his order, the agent for his affairs was Chinnappa-Rāya,—by order of whose agent Manikayya, and the order of Malla[pa]ya, the seṭṭis, gauḍas and all the subjects remitted for all castes the tax on marriages and on marriage pandals. text.location: At the same village, or a stone built into the south wall of the raṅga-maṇṭapa of the Īśvara temple.
text.remarks:
Obeisance to S'ambhū &c. Be it well. (On the date specified),—when the mahārājādhirāja
rāja-paramêśvara, master of the eastern southern and western oceans, vira-pratāpa Achyuta-Dêva-
Rāya-mahārāya was ruling the kingdom of the world :—by his order, the agent for his affairs was
Chinnappa-Rāya,—by order of whose agent Manikayya, and the order of Malla[pa]ya, the seṭṭis,
gauḍas and all the subjects remitted for all castes the tax on marriages and on marriage pandals.

cells.location: *At Hirê-Yammiḍanûru (Bharamanâvakanadurga hobli), on a stone standing against the south*
cells.remarks: Obeisance to S'ambhu &c. The Châlukyas ruled the ocean-girdled earth : after them the Kaḷa- churyya king Bijjaṇa protected the earth. At whose beginning the king Taḷatta Pândya protected with affection the Noṇambavâḍi Thirty-two Thousand, which is like a girdle for the young woman the Earth. After him Phonli-Pândya was celebrated, and after him . . . . . was born Râya-Pândya. After him, to king Noḷeya-Pândya was born . . . . . the king Kâma-Dêva. Kâmarasa's son, devoted 1g Holalkere Taluq to war, . . . . ruled the earth in succession, an ornament of kings. Thrashing the line of Pândya kings on the field of battle, terrifying and putting to flight hostile kings, by the might of his arm, the crest-jewel of righteous rulers, the Hoysaḷa king vira-Baḷḷāḷa ruled the celebrated Noṇambavāḍi. (Here follows the usual account of the rise and succession of the Hoysalas, to Narasimha). In the Pândya-nâḍ, which was great in the world in gifts and sacrifices, pre-eminent was the Emmeganûr-vṛitti, brilliant as a mirror set with jewels. Description of its groves and gardens. The place of residence (*nelemane*) for that vṛitti, an abode of fortune, Emmeganûr shone like Amarâvati, the city of Dêvêndra. The descent of its *manmeyas* was as follows :—Reckoned as a wrestler in war was Vaijarasa, whose son was Bammarasa, whose eldest son was Hariparasa. These being the masters of Emmeganûr, those excellent *manmeyas* did service to the former rulers who put down the evil and protected the good. Be it well. When, (with usual titles), the Hoysaḷa king vira-Narasimha-Dêva was in the residence of Dôrasamudra, ruling the kingdom in peace and wisdom :—A dweller at his lotus feet (with praises) was Rebbacha. (Some part effaced here). Apparently praises of certain officers of the palace, two brothers named Râghava and S'ankara, who ? were Nolambas. His family god Sômânaṭha, his mother . . . . . le, of the Bhâradvâja-gôtra, [ornament of the] twice-born, was Râghava, whose brother was S'ankara;—how fortunate was he. In the Emmeganûr-vṛitti, in the royal city (*râjadhâni*) Emmeganûr, (with praises), was Jakkarasa, a promoter of the race of the twice-born. To Jakkarasa's mother were born the brothers Holali-dêva, Dêvapa, and Kali-dêva, how fortunate thus was Rudra, whose chief *mâta* was Harihara. Then follow praises of Biyâḷa Mâḷi-seṭṭi, born to Bammi-seṭṭi and Kâdave, stating how he acquired the name Biyâḷa. In Emmeganûr, famous in the world, Biyâḷa Gêti-seṭṭi was famous. Thus the master of Emmeganûr, Jakkarasa, Biyâḷa Gêti-seṭṭi, Kêta-gauḍa and numerous other gauḍas and seṭṭis (named)—all these prabhu-gaudas, headed by the adhikâri Râghava-dêva and Pampayya, (on the date specified), at the time of the sun's eclipse, for the decorations and illumina- tions of the god Svayambhu Kali of Hiri-Yemmiganûr, for vessels, cloths, Chaitra, pavitra, and temple repairs, made a grant of Handiganahaḷḷi, washing the feet of (with the usual ascetic virtues) Amritarâsi's son Bhimarâsi's son Brahmâsivamâla-guru. Boundaries. Be it well. Of the Gangânvaya praised in all the world, (with various epithets, including) lord of Nandagiri, nanniya-Ganga, jayaduttaranga, having the crest of a rutting elephant, kaṇṇambi- nâtha,—to Hariyarasa . . . . was born Bammarasa-Dêva, who, washing the feet of Bhûnarâsi-guru, formerly made the following grant. (Here come the details). And the Pândya-nâḍ hejjunka heggaḍe Ruddayya a made a grant (specified) for the perpetual light of the same god from the grain duties of the Emmeganûr-vṛitti, and one oil-mill. And the Ojas of 12 villages made a grant (specified) for the same purpose. Usual final verses.

text.location: *At Hirê-Yammiḍanûru (Bharamanâvakanadurga hobli), on a stone standing against the south*
text.remarks:
Obeisance to S'ambhu &c. The Châlukyas ruled the ocean-girdled earth : after them the Kaḷa-
churyya king Bijjaṇa protected the earth. At whose beginning the king Taḷatta Pândya protected
with affection the Noṇambavâḍi Thirty-two Thousand, which is like a girdle for the young woman the
Earth. After him Phonli-Pândya was celebrated, and after him . . . . . was born Râya-Pândya.
After him, to king Noḷeya-Pândya was born . . . . . the king Kâma-Dêva. Kâmarasa's son, devoted
1g

Holalkere Taluq

to war, . . . . ruled the earth in succession, an ornament of kings. Thrashing the line of Pândya
kings on the field of battle, terrifying and putting to flight hostile kings, by the might of his arm,
the crest-jewel of righteous rulers, the Hoysaḷa king vira-Baḷḷāḷa ruled the celebrated Noṇambavāḍi.
(Here follows the usual account of the rise and succession of the Hoysalas, to Narasimha).

In the Pândya-nâḍ, which was great in the world in gifts and sacrifices, pre-eminent was the
Emmeganûr-vṛitti, brilliant as a mirror set with jewels. Description of its groves and gardens. The
place of residence (*nelemane*) for that vṛitti, an abode of fortune, Emmeganûr shone like Amarâvati,
the city of Dêvêndra. The descent of its *manmeyas* was as follows :—Reckoned as a wrestler in war
was Vaijarasa, whose son was Bammarasa, whose eldest son was Hariparasa. These being the masters
of Emmeganûr, those excellent *manmeyas* did service to the former rulers who put down the evil and
protected the good.

Be it well. When, (with usual titles), the Hoysaḷa king vira-Narasimha-Dêva was in the
residence of Dôrasamudra, ruling the kingdom in peace and wisdom :—A dweller at his lotus feet
(with praises) was Rebbacha. (Some part effaced here). Apparently praises of certain officers of the
palace, two brothers named Râghava and S'ankara, who ? were Nolambas. His family god Sômânaṭha,
his mother . . . . . le, of the Bhâradvâja-gôtra, [ornament of the] twice-born, was Râghava, whose
brother was S'ankara;—how fortunate was he. In the Emmeganûr-vṛitti, in the royal city (*râjadhâni*)
Emmeganûr, (with praises), was Jakkarasa, a promoter of the race of the twice-born. To Jakkarasa's
mother were born the brothers Holali-dêva, Dêvapa, and Kali-dêva, how fortunate thus was Rudra,
whose chief *mâta* was Harihara. Then follow praises of Biyâḷa Mâḷi-seṭṭi, born to Bammi-seṭṭi
and Kâdave, stating how he acquired the name Biyâḷa. In Emmeganûr, famous in the world, Biyâḷa
Gêti-seṭṭi was famous.

Thus the master of Emmeganûr, Jakkarasa, Biyâḷa Gêti-seṭṭi, Kêta-gauḍa and numerous other
gauḍas and seṭṭis (named)—all these prabhu-gaudas, headed by the adhikâri Râghava-dêva and
Pampayya, (on the date specified), at the time of the sun's eclipse, for the decorations and illumina-
tions of the god Svayambhu Kali of Hiri-Yemmiganûr, for vessels, cloths, Chaitra, pavitra, and
temple repairs, made a grant of Handiganahaḷḷi, washing the feet of (with the usual ascetic virtues)
Amritarâsi's son Bhimarâsi's son Brahmâsivamâla-guru. Boundaries.

Be it well. Of the Gangânvaya praised in all the world, (with various epithets, including) lord of
Nandagiri, nanniya-Ganga, jayaduttaranga, having the crest of a rutting elephant, kaṇṇambi-
nâtha,—to Hariyarasa . . . . was born Bammarasa-Dêva, who, washing the feet of Bhûnarâsi-guru,
formerly made the following grant. (Here come the details).

And the Pândya-nâḍ hejjunka heggaḍe Ruddayya a made a grant (specified) for the perpetual
light of the same god from the grain duties of the Emmeganûr-vṛitti, and one oil-mill. And the
Ojas of 12 villages made a grant (specified) for the same purpose.

cells.remarks: Obeisance to S'ambhu &c. Obeisance to Gaṇapati. Be it well. When, (with usual Chalukya titles), Tribhuvanamalla-Dêva's victorious kingdom was extending &c :— Holalkere Taluq And, a dweller at his lotus feet,—Be it well. Entitled to the band of five chief instruments, mahā-maṇḍalēśvara, boon lord of Kāñchī-pura, sun in the sky of the Yadu-vaṁśa, (with other epi_ thets, including) champion in cutting on both sides, defeater of the desigins of Rājiga-Chōḷa,—Tri- bhuvanamalla-Pāṇḍya-Dēva was ruling the Noḷambavāḍi Thirty-two Thousand kingdom in peace and wisdom ;— Be it well. Born in the Gangānvaya famous in all the world, Konguṇivarmma-dharmma- mahārājādhirāja, (with numerous other epithets, including) boon lord of Kōlāla-pura, lord of Nanda- giri, nanniya Ganga, jayad-uttaranga, having the crest of a rutting elephant, his father's shining sword (*ayyana chandrahāsa*),—with these and all other titles, was the mahā-maṇḍalēśvara Gaug- arasa.— A dweller at his lotus feet, the Guṇjigaṇūr prabhu-gāvuṇḍa, the potter Bommaṇa, having taken a strict vow (*vīra-brata*) not to anoint the head or eat food till he had set up the god Kumbēśvara,— for the decorations of the god, perpetual lamp, and offerings, made grants of land (specified). Gangarasa, ruling the Kukkavāḍi Three Hundred, halted and (on the date specified), washing the feet of Uttamarāśi-paṇḍita, made the grant. Imprecations. Footnote 1. The meaning of this and other terms used is not clearly understood.

Local exemptions according to former custom. Usual final verses.

Obeisance to S'ambhu &c. Be it well. (On the date specified), the mahâ-nâyakâchâryya Kâma-
geti-Kastûri-Medakeri-Nâyakarayya caused to be written and given to the Bâgûr chiranti, Chenna-
Basappa-dêva, the town lands of Guṇdasamudra in the Bâgûr-sime, including the wet land, dry
land, houses . . . the whole free of all imposts. Whoso causes this to fail,—if Karnnâṭas, will be
guilty of killing cows in Kâsi; if Musalmâns, of killing pigs in Mecca. Those who maintain it

cells.remarks: (Nāgari characters). Obeisance to Gaṇādhipati. Praise of S'ambhu, the Boar and Gaṇéśa. From the churning of the milk ocean by the gods arose a bright one (Chandra), disperser of darkness. His son, distinguished for great penance, was Budha. From him sprang Purûrava; from him, Âyu; from Âyu, Nahusha; from him, Yayâti, great in war; from whom, Dêvayâni, was born the famous Turvasu, the equal of Vasu. In that race arose Timma-bhūpati, as renowned among the Tuluva kings as Krishna was in the Yadu line, whose wife was Dêvaki. From him sprang Īsvara, whose wife was Bukkamā. From him was Narasa, like Kâma, the joy of Dêvaki. Quickly damming the Kâvêri when in full flood, he crossed over, and seizing the enemy alive, took possession of his kingdom and of the city S'rirangapaṭṭaṇa, and erected a pillar of victory. Having conquered Chêra, Chôla, and Pâṇḍya, together with the lord of Madhurâ, whose honour was his ornament, the fierce Turushka, the Gajapati king and others,—he imposed his commands on the heads of all the famous kings from the banks of the Ganges to Lanka (Ceylon); and from the rising to the setting sun. (Omitting laudations);—From Tippâji and Nāgalâ-Dêvi were born to him Nṛisimha and Krishna-Râya. The heroic Nṛasimha, seated on the jewel-throne in Vijayanagara, by his fame and policy putting to shame Nriga, Nala, Nahusha and other kings of the earth, ruled the kingdom from Sêtu to Sumêru and from the eastern to the western mountains, drawing the hearts of all to himself. All manner of gifts did he make in Kanakasadas (Chidambram), in the temple of Virûpâksha (at Hampi), in the town of Kâlahasti (North Arcot District), in Venkaṭâdri (at Tirupati), in Kânchî (Conjeevaram), in S'rîsaila (Karnul District), in S'ôṇasaila (Tiruvannâmalai), in the great Harihara (Chitaldroog District), in Ahôbala (Karnul District), in Sangama (at the junction of the Malâpahâri and Krishnâ), in S'riranga (near Trichinopoly), in Kumbhaghôṇa (Tanjore District), in the Mahâ-nandi-tîrtha (Karnul District), in Nivritti (at the junction of the Tungabhadrâ and Krishnâ), in Gôkarṇa (North Kanara District), in Râmasêtu (Madura District), and many other sacred places,—namely, every variety of the great gifts, such as the golden egg, the golden wheel, the goldon pot, the goldon cow, the seven golden seas, the wishing tree, the golden cow of plenty, golden earth, gold horse-chariot, a man's weight in gold, a thousand cows, a golden horse, the golden-wombed (Brahma), gold elephant-chariot, and the five ploughs. Having ruled a kingdom unopposed, this king of the earth, famed for his virtues, went to svarga, as if to rule the kingdom of the sky. Mightier even than him, the king Krishna-Râya took the earth upon his shoulders as if a jewelled epaulette. From his wide-spread fame all nature became as if of the same (white) colour, so that Purâri (S'iva) could be distinguished only by the eye in his forehead, Padmaksha (Vishnu) by his four arms, Padmabhû (Brahma) by his four faces, Kâli by her sword, Ramâ (Lakshmi) by her lotus, Vâṇî (Sarasvati) by the lute in her hand. Overcome by his glory, the sun sinks into the western ocean as if quite unable to endure the distress of mind. As if fearing that the seven oceans would provide a refuge to his enemies, they were dried up with the clouds of dust raised by the earth trampled to pieces by the troops of his horsemen, but they were formed again by the measureless streams poured out with the brahmâṇḍa, svarṇa-mêru, and other his great gifts. As though, in order that the donations and wealth he had given might be long enjoyed, he would stay the chariot of the sun and provide resting places for the gods, he erected pillars, stretching like mountain peaks into the sky, filled with the accounts of his victorious expeditions to each point of the compass Holsalkere Taluq and with the names of his titles. In Kânchi, Sîrîsaila, S'ônâchala, Kanakasabhâ, Venkatâdri and other places, so as to ald greatly to his glory, did he again and again bestow the great gifts de- scribed in the śâstras, together with the grants associated with them. Punisher of warlike kings, able in protecting the world which lies in the arms of S'êsha, punisher of kings who break their word, giver of joy to his dependents, fierec in war, styled râjâdhirâja râja-paramêsvara, Suratråna of the Hindu kings, destroyer of the tigers the evil, a ganda-bhêrunda, distinguished by these and other titles; served by Anga, Vanga, Kalinga, and other kings, with such words as “Look on us, great king! Victory! Long life !”—his geneo-ity praised by the learned, this king of kings Krishna- Raya, seated on the jewel throne in Vijayanagara, shone with surpassing fame. (On the date specified), on the bank of the Tungabhadra river, in the presence of Virûpâksha, desiring to form an agrahâra, with full affection he gave to Timmâ-bhatta praised in every way, ever regular in the śrânta and smârtha ceremonies, a chief Brahman worthy of a grant of land, the son of the learned Lingâ-bhatta, descended from Oruganţa Kâkapedda, of the S'aunakânvaya, Apastamba-sûtra and Yajuś-śâkhâ, - the Bobûr village (boundary villages specified), situated in the Maleyanûr-sthala, in the Hiriyûr-śîma of the Kuntala-dêśa, - together with its hamlets Hátadorai, Ganadahunişe and Nâmânpalle, (with all the usual rights). And this proprietor, dividing it into 32 shares, reserved 16 for himself as manager, and the remainder he bestowed on the Brahmans (named). The boundaries of the agrahara are here written in the language of the country. (Here follow the details). This copper śâsana of a grant of land by the renowned king Krishna-Râya, was composed with soft expressions by Sabhapati at the command of Krishna-Dêva-mahârâya. And by order of Krishna- Dêva-mahârâya the copper śâsana was engraved by Mallana's son, the carpenter Virapicharya. Usual final verses. (Signed)-śri-Virûpâksha

text.location: *At Mattôdu (Hosadurga hobli), on copper plates in possession of Narasamma.*
text.remarks:
(Nāgari characters).
Obeisance to Gaṇādhipati. Praise of S'ambhu, the Boar and Gaṇéśa.
From the churning of the milk ocean by the gods arose a bright one (Chandra), disperser of darkness. His son, distinguished for great penance, was Budha. From him sprang Purûrava; from him, Âyu; from Âyu, Nahusha; from him, Yayâti, great in war; from whom, Dêvayâni, was born the famous Turvasu, the equal of Vasu.

In that race arose Timma-bhūpati, as renowned among the Tuluva kings as Krishna was in the Yadu line, whose wife was Dêvaki. From him sprang Īsvara, whose wife was Bukkamā. From him was Narasa, like Kâma, the joy of Dêvaki. Quickly damming the Kâvêri when in full flood, he crossed over, and seizing the enemy alive, took possession of his kingdom and of the city S'rirangapaṭṭaṇa, and erected a pillar of victory. Having conquered Chêra, Chôla, and Pâṇḍya, together with the lord of Madhurâ, whose honour was his ornament, the fierce Turushka, the Gajapati king and others,—he imposed his commands on the heads of all the famous kings from the banks of the Ganges to Lanka (Ceylon); and from the rising to the setting sun. (Omitting laudations);—From Tippâji and Nāgalâ-Dêvi were born to him Nṛisimha and Krishna-Râya.

The heroic Nṛasimha, seated on the jewel-throne in Vijayanagara, by his fame and policy putting to shame Nriga, Nala, Nahusha and other kings of the earth, ruled the kingdom from Sêtu to Sumêru and from the eastern to the western mountains, drawing the hearts of all to himself. All manner of gifts did he make in Kanakasadas (Chidambram), in the temple of Virûpâksha (at Hampi), in the town of Kâlahasti (North Arcot District), in Venkaṭâdri (at Tirupati), in Kânchî (Conjeevaram), in S'rîsaila (Karnul District), in S'ôṇasaila (Tiruvannâmalai), in the great Harihara (Chitaldroog District), in Ahôbala (Karnul District), in Sangama (at the junction of the Malâpahâri and Krishnâ), in S'riranga (near Trichinopoly), in Kumbhaghôṇa (Tanjore District), in the Mahâ-nandi-tîrtha (Karnul District), in Nivritti (at the junction of the Tungabhadrâ and Krishnâ), in Gôkarṇa (North Kanara District), in Râmasêtu (Madura District), and many other sacred places,—namely, every variety of the great gifts, such as the golden egg, the golden wheel, the goldon pot, the goldon cow, the seven golden seas, the wishing tree, the golden cow of plenty, golden earth, gold horse-chariot, a man's weight in gold, a thousand cows, a golden horse, the golden-wombed (Brahma), gold elephant-chariot, and the five ploughs. Having ruled a kingdom unopposed, this king of the earth, famed for his virtues, went to svarga, as if to rule the kingdom of the sky.

Mightier even than him, the king Krishna-Râya took the earth upon his shoulders as if a jewelled epaulette. From his wide-spread fame all nature became as if of the same (white) colour, so that Purâri (S'iva) could be distinguished only by the eye in his forehead, Padmaksha (Vishnu) by his four arms, Padmabhû (Brahma) by his four faces, Kâli by her sword, Ramâ (Lakshmi) by her lotus, Vâṇî (Sarasvati) by the lute in her hand. Overcome by his glory, the sun sinks into the western ocean as if quite unable to endure the distress of mind. As if fearing that the seven oceans would provide a refuge to his enemies, they were dried up with the clouds of dust raised by the earth trampled to pieces by the troops of his horsemen, but they were formed again by the measureless streams poured out with the brahmâṇḍa, svarṇa-mêru, and other his great gifts. As though, in order that the donations and wealth he had given might be long enjoyed, he would stay the chariot of the sun and provide resting places for the gods, he erected pillars, stretching like mountain peaks into the sky, filled with the accounts of his victorious expeditions to each point of the compass

Holsalkere Taluq
and with the names of his titles. In Kânchi, Sîrîsaila, S'ônâchala, Kanakasabhâ, Venkatâdri and
other places, so as to ald greatly to his glory, did he again and again bestow the great gifts de-
scribed in the śâstras, together with the grants associated with them. Punisher of warlike kings,
able in protecting the world which lies in the arms of S'êsha, punisher of kings who break their
word, giver of joy to his dependents, fierec in war, styled râjâdhirâja râja-paramêsvara, Suratråna
of the Hindu kings, destroyer of the tigers the evil, a ganda-bhêrunda, distinguished by these
and other titles; served by Anga, Vanga, Kalinga, and other kings, with such words as “Look on
us, great king! Victory! Long life !”—his geneo-ity praised by the learned, this king of kings Krishna-
Raya, seated on the jewel throne in Vijayanagara, shone with surpassing fame.

(On the date specified), on the bank of the Tungabhadra river, in the presence of Virûpâksha,
desiring to form an agrahâra, with full affection he gave to Timmâ-bhatta praised in every way, ever
regular in the śrânta and smârtha ceremonies, a chief Brahman worthy of a grant of land, the
son of the learned Lingâ-bhatta, descended from Oruganţa Kâkapedda, of the S'aunakânvaya,
Apastamba-sûtra and Yajuś-śâkhâ, - the Bobûr village (boundary villages specified), situated in the
Maleyanûr-sthala, in the Hiriyûr-śîma of the Kuntala-dêśa, - together with its hamlets Hátadorai,
Ganadahunişe and Nâmânpalle, (with all the usual rights).

And this proprietor, dividing it into 32 shares, reserved 16 for himself as manager, and the
remainder he bestowed on the Brahmans (named). The boundaries of the agrahara are here written
in the language of the country. (Here follow the details).

This copper śâsana of a grant of land by the renowned king Krishna-Râya, was composed with
soft expressions by Sabhapati at the command of Krishna-Dêva-mahârâya. And by order of Krishna-
Dêva-mahârâya the copper śâsana was engraved by Mallana's son, the carpenter Virapicharya.

cells.remarks: (Nāgari characters). Obeisance to Ganadhipati. Praise of S'ambhu, the Boar and Ganêśa. There was a râjâdhirâja, of the Manumala-kula, handsome and high-born, the king named Hâl- appa, versed in the śaiva śâstras. Having given gold and clothing in the days of Harihara, his fame was celebrated by the twice-born, in valour the equal of S'akra, his countenance like the moon, the punisher of all enemies. In the city named Mattêdu dwelt the king Hâla, the walls of whose palace were like gold (in colour), adorned with all manner of paintings. His son was the king named Doddana, mighty in valour, who gave to Hiriyanna, the councillor of his family, Ganjagéra. Râma.. having said to him, “Make an agrahâra, with a tank of pure water,”-he accordingly made it an agrahâra, and setting up broad stones bearing the figure of Vamana at the boundaries, established the Ganjagéra agrahâra, putting up also a stone in the village, to the east, in the presence of the Son of the Wind (Hanuman), containing the account. The income from the village was 20 nishkas. All rights to be enjoyed free of all taxes. The king Doddana-Nâyaka's son was Saigapa, who ruled the earth for a long time in righteous- ness, and the Brahmans settled in Mattinâdu strove by good works to increase his fame, and dwelt there in great comfort. Holalkere Taluq His son Hâla-Râja, when going to the forest to hunt wild beasts, saw the Gañjagêra agrahâra in ruins, and the fine tank breached. Having slain many tigers and fierce wild boars, he freed the forest so that it might be traversed without fear. On returning to the city with his forces, he informed the matter to his wife and his two sons Siddharâma and Doddanna, saying; "O sons, the agrahâra was formerly made by my father's father. It must be done by us if we wish the work of merit to be maintained." Hearing these words of beloved father, they said, "Let it be as you say, and let the work of merit be maintained." The king (thereupon) immediately sent for Hiriyanna and Râmachandra, and gave them orders, saying, "Make the agrahâra and the tank (again)," and informed Râmachandra, that for his own welfare, would give the land in writing to Brahmans. Hiriyanna and Râmachandra, having heard the words of the king, (re)made the large fine tank; and (on the date specified), at S'iva-râtri, in order that he might in the other world gain the lotus feet of the First Being, the king gave a sâsana for Gañjagêra-pura, changing his former name to Nara- sâpura. (Here follows a list of the Brahmans who received shares)—altogether 16. (List of the boundary stones, in the language of the country),—altogether 10. Usual final verses.

text.remarks:
(Nāgari characters).

Obeisance to Ganadhipati. Praise of S'ambhu, the Boar and Ganêśa.

There was a râjâdhirâja, of the Manumala-kula, handsome and high-born, the king named Hâl-
appa, versed in the śaiva śâstras. Having given gold and clothing in the days of Harihara, his fame
was celebrated by the twice-born, in valour the equal of S'akra, his countenance like the moon, the
punisher of all enemies. In the city named Mattêdu dwelt the king Hâla, the walls of whose palace
were like gold (in colour), adorned with all manner of paintings. His son was the king named
Doddana, mighty in valour, who gave to Hiriyanna, the councillor of his family, Ganjagéra. Râma..
having said to him, “Make an agrahâra, with a tank of pure water,”-he accordingly made it an
agrahâra, and setting up broad stones bearing the figure of Vamana at the boundaries, established
the Ganjagéra agrahâra, putting up also a stone in the village, to the east, in the presence of the Son
of the Wind (Hanuman), containing the account. The income from the village was 20 nishkas. All
rights to be enjoyed free of all taxes.

The king Doddana-Nâyaka's son was Saigapa, who ruled the earth for a long time in righteous-
ness, and the Brahmans settled in Mattinâdu strove by good works to increase his fame, and dwelt
there in great comfort.

Holalkere Taluq

His son Hâla-Râja, when going to the forest to hunt wild beasts, saw the Gañjagêra agrahâra in
ruins, and the fine tank breached. Having slain many tigers and fierce wild boars, he freed the forest
so that it might be traversed without fear. On returning to the city with his forces, he informed the
matter to his wife and his two sons Siddharâma and Doddanna, saying; "O sons, the agrahâra was
formerly made by my father's father. It must be done by us if we wish the work of merit to be
maintained." Hearing these words of beloved father, they said, "Let it be as you say, and
let the work of merit be maintained." The king (thereupon) immediately sent for Hiriyanna and
Râmachandra, and gave them orders, saying, "Make the agrahâra and the tank (again)," and
informed Râmachandra, that for his own welfare, would give the land in writing to Brahmans.

Hiriyanna and Râmachandra, having heard the words of the king, (re)made the large fine tank;
and (on the date specified), at S'iva-râtri, in order that he might in the other world gain the lotus
feet of the First Being, the king gave a sâsana for Gañjagêra-pura, changing his former name to Nara-
sâpura. (Here follows a list of the Brahmans who received shares)—altogether 16. (List of the
boundary stones, in the language of the country),—altogether 10. Usual final verses.Read more (3 KB)

cells.location: At Hunuvinôḍu (Hosadurga hobli), on a stone to the north of the Nârâyaṇa temple.
cells.remarks: Obeisance to S'ambhu &c. Be it well. Entitled to the band of five chief instruments, mahâ- maṇḍalêśvara, boon lord of Dvâravatî-pura, sun in the sky of the Yâdava-kula, crest-jewel of per- fection, Râja of the Male-Râjas, champion over the Malapar,—adorned with these and many other names, the mahâ-maṇḍalêśvara Tribhuvanamalla vîra-Vishṇuvarddhana-Hoysaṇa-Dêva's valour was as follows ;—Chôla's scarecrow, Mâlava's cutthroat, a Mâkâli to pursue and devour Chôla, a rutting elephant to trample on Kaḷinga, an arrow in the bowels of Khacha, a whip for the back of Nêpâla, was he ; such was the terror that the king vîra-Vishṇu produced among hostile kings. Nangali, Koṅgu, Siṅghamale, Râyapuram, Taḷakâḍu, Rodda, the Chengiri abode, Kollagiri, Baḷḷare, Valluru, Chakragoṭṭa, Uchchaṅgi, Virâṭa's city, Bankapura, Banavâse, Koyatûr, did the famous warrior, the brave Vishṇuvarddhana capture. His eldest son's valour was as follows :-description of his fighting . . . . . When the mahâ-maṇḍalêśvara, capturer of Talakâḍu, Koṅgu, Naṅgali, Gaṅgavâḍi, Nonamba- vâḍi, Banavâse and Hânungallu, the bhujabala-pratâpa, unassisted here, nissanka-pratâpa Hoysaṇa vîra-Ballâla-Dêva, protecting the Gangavâḍi Ninety-six Thousand, was in the residence of Dôra- samudra, ruling the kingdom in peace and wisdom :- A dweller at his lotus feet, the mahâ-sâmantâdhipati, the grinder of feudaṭories, Nirugunda Chaṭṭeya-Nâyaka's valour and glory were as follows ;-May Harihara (with praises) grant long life, wealth and victory to sâmanta-Chaṭṭam as long as sun and moon and star endure. (Verses describing his exploits, much defaced). The numberless army of Pâṇḍya he completely trampled down.-In the province which he was ruling was Mâdi-Sêṭṭi . . . . . . . . . . . . . Be it well. Lineally descended âchâryya of the earth disciplined by the Harihara, Hiranya- garbha and others the five hundred systems praised in all worlds, head-jewel in Jambu-dvîpa to the Five hundred svâmis and the seven and a half and eleven and a half (? castes), a form of glory to all in Sirâḷamalige Santesâsana.. and Nirggunda-nâḍ, increaser of the sameya-dharmma (or caste piety), helper of other sameyas (or castes), wronger of those who wrong, punisher of those who commit faults,— the mahâ-nâlprabhu Vommanakchi Mâra-Sêṭṭi, for the decorations of the god Mârêśvara of Desiyapaṭṭa- ṇa Santesâsana Sirâḷamalige and Hâḷigaṇoḍu in Arambala-nâḍ, for the worship, repeated ceremonies, offerings, perpetual light and temple repairs, (on the date specified), at the time of the eclipse of the sun, made over to the âchâryya Masaṇa-jîya the lands (specified), with usual rights. Usual final verses. The god Mârêśvara is the refuge.

text.location: At Hunuvinôḍu (Hosadurga hobli), on a stone to the north of the Nârâyaṇa temple.
text.remarks:
Obeisance to S'ambhu &c. Be it well. Entitled to the band of five chief instruments, mahâ-
maṇḍalêśvara, boon lord of Dvâravatî-pura, sun in the sky of the Yâdava-kula, crest-jewel of per-
fection, Râja of the Male-Râjas, champion over the Malapar,—adorned with these and many other
names, the mahâ-maṇḍalêśvara Tribhuvanamalla vîra-Vishṇuvarddhana-Hoysaṇa-Dêva's valour was
as follows ;—Chôla's scarecrow, Mâlava's cutthroat, a Mâkâli to pursue and devour Chôla, a rutting
elephant to trample on Kaḷinga, an arrow in the bowels of Khacha, a whip for the back of Nêpâla,
was he ; such was the terror that the king vîra-Vishṇu produced among hostile kings. Nangali,
Koṅgu, Siṅghamale, Râyapuram, Taḷakâḍu, Rodda, the Chengiri abode, Kollagiri, Baḷḷare, Valluru,
Chakragoṭṭa, Uchchaṅgi, Virâṭa's city, Bankapura, Banavâse, Koyatûr, did the famous warrior, the
brave Vishṇuvarddhana capture. His eldest son's valour was as follows :-description of his
fighting . . . . .
When the mahâ-maṇḍalêśvara, capturer of Talakâḍu, Koṅgu, Naṅgali, Gaṅgavâḍi, Nonamba-
vâḍi, Banavâse and Hânungallu, the bhujabala-pratâpa, unassisted here, nissanka-pratâpa Hoysaṇa
vîra-Ballâla-Dêva, protecting the Gangavâḍi Ninety-six Thousand, was in the residence of Dôra-
samudra, ruling the kingdom in peace and wisdom :-
A dweller at his lotus feet, the mahâ-sâmantâdhipati, the grinder of feudaṭories, Nirugunda
Chaṭṭeya-Nâyaka's valour and glory were as follows ;-May Harihara (with praises) grant long life,
wealth and victory to sâmanta-Chaṭṭam as long as sun and moon and star endure. (Verses describing
his exploits, much defaced). The numberless army of Pâṇḍya he completely trampled down.-In
the province which he was ruling was Mâdi-Sêṭṭi . . . . . . . . . . . . .
Be it well. Lineally descended âchâryya of the earth disciplined by the Harihara, Hiranya-
garbha and others the five hundred systems praised in all worlds, head-jewel in Jambu-dvîpa to
the Five hundred svâmis and the seven and a half and eleven and a half (? castes), a form of glory to
all in Sirâḷamalige Santesâsana.. and Nirggunda-nâḍ, increaser of the sameya-dharmma (or caste piety),
helper of other sameyas (or castes), wronger of those who wrong, punisher of those who commit faults,—
the mahâ-nâlprabhu Vommanakchi Mâra-Sêṭṭi, for the decorations of the god Mârêśvara of Desiyapaṭṭa-
ṇa Santesâsana Sirâḷamalige and Hâḷigaṇoḍu in Arambala-nâḍ, for the worship, repeated ceremonies,
offerings, perpetual light and temple repairs, (on the date specified), at the time of the eclipse of
the sun, made over to the âchâryya Masaṇa-jîya the lands (specified), with usual rights.
Usual final verses.

cells.location: *At Bâgûr (Bâgûr hobli), on a stone at the village gate.*
cells.remarks: The feet of the god Mallikârjuna of Śrīsaila are the refuge. Obeisance to S'ambhu &c. (On the date specified), when the mahârâjâdhirâja râja-paramêśvara vīra-pratâpa vīra-Sadâśiva-Râya- mahârâya was ruling the kingdom of the world in peace and wisdom :—he gave orders to Râma-Râja- ayya, saying “ We have given up to the barbers, tax, fixed rent, forced labour, *birâda*, customs, toll for watchmen, these and other dues, free of all imposts.—On which he informed Eṛe-Krishnappa- Nâkaya, saying ” In your Bâgûr-sîme we have given to the barbers the same privileges (repeated).— And in token of this remission and the approval of the gauḍas and sênabôvas of Bâgûr-sîme, and the subjects of the two sîmes, this *mânya-śāsana* was erected. Imprecation. He who obtained the remission of the taxes was Koṇḍôja of Vijayanagari.

(On the date specified), when the mahâ- maṇḍalêśvara râjâdhirâja râja-paramêśvara vīra-pratâpa Sadâśiva-Râya was ruling a peaceful king- dom :—and Pôtappa-Nâkayya's (son) Krishnappa-Nâkaya's agent Viṭhaṇa-Nâkaya was holding the Hoḷalkere Taluq pārupatya of the Bâgûr-śime,—the outer pêṭhe being in ruins,—Nârasimmaiya of the customs made petition to Vithana-Nâyaka,—whereupon he sent for Liṅgaṇa-gauḍa and many others (named), all the subjects, directed them to have the pêṭhe built, giving it another name of Krishnâ- pura after Era-Krishnappa-Nâkayya, and populate it. Those who settle there will be free of all taxes for one year from the time they come; after that they will not only be included in the family agreement, but if they have taken possession, we and the subjects will give up (our claim). cells.remarks: (On the date specified), the village of ...... otherwise called Krishnasamudra,—Era-Krish- nappa-Kâyaka, in order that merit might accrue to Sadâśiva-Râya, made over to (the god) Chenniga- Râya. Three Brahmans named who were to conduct the services in the presence of the god, one of the three always remaining in the village in Bâgûr; and at the pancha-parva and other great festivals, four were to conduct the services. cells.location: *At Honnekere (Bâgûr hobli), on a stone near the Kallēśvara temple.*
cells.remarks: Hojalkere Taluq pion over those who say they are such and such,¹ subduer of the elephant army, son of Mali-Dêvi and Vīra-Dêvarasa,—Vallabha-Râya-mahârâja,—by his order, his man (manushya) Peddarasa had it made. And in order that *dharma* might be confirmed to that Vīra-Dêvarasa, he made grants of land (specified) for the offerings of the god Kêśava, to continue as long as sun and moon. Imprec- ation. Usual final verses. To Sirigiri .... châryya who did this work, the king, farmers and subjects, agreeing together, made a grant for ever of 8 *kolaga*. Imprecation. *Date 1515 A.D.* (On the date specified),—in order that merit might accrue to Krishna-Râya-mahârâja,—for the chatra of the god Mallikârjuna, Muluvâgil Mallinâtharasa's (or Nâgarasa's)² son Bâgûr Malla- rasa granted the village of Âlahalli. (The grant is repeated). Usual final verses. *Date 1226 A.D.* Obeisances to S'ambhu &c. Be it well. When, (with usual titles), Hoysala vîra-Nârasimha- Dêva, protecting the Gangavâdi Ninety-six Thousand and the Noḷambavâdi Thrity-two Thousand, was in the residence of Dôrasamudra, ruling the kingdom in peace and wisdom :—(On the date specified), the 9th year from his assuming the crown, the year Pârtthiva &c.,—certain gauḍas (named) of Maṇali, which is Kêśavapura, fighting with various persons (named) of Hati and Santeya- suri, died,—and the celestial nymphs bore them away in flowery cars to the highest *svarga*, showing them the city of Kailâsa and the feet of Mahêsvara, and seating them on the thrones of heroes. And on account of the departure (or death) of Mâdi-gauḍa, certain gauḍas (named) granted *umbali* for the god Kali, for the sake of a *bîraga-liṁga*. *Date 1237 A.D.* Obeisance to S'ambhu &c. Be it well. When the pratâpa-cakravartti Hoysala vîra-Sômêsvara- Dêvarasa was ruling the kingdom in peace :—(on the date specified), when Mâvinahaḷḷi Mâdaya and .... yahalli Maleya-Nâyaka carried off the cows, Jaka-bôva (fought) and gained the world of *svarga*. Mâra-bôva set up this stone for him. *Date 1533 A.D.* *(Nâgari characters.)* (Corresponds with No. 94 above, as far as the date of that.) His generosity praised by the learn- ed, this king of kings, Krishna-Râya, established on the jewel-throne in Vijayanagara, daily sur- passing Nriga and all others, shone in the power of good fortune and the fullness of fame, from the eastern to the western mountains and from the extremity of Hêmâchala to Sêtu. The world of gods having been taken as his portion by Krishna-Râya, after him his younger brother of meritorious deeds, king Achyuta, took the world of the earth for his portion, subduing his enemies, surpassing Indra, and bestowing their desires on the learned. The moon of his fame moves in the world in all the tithi, and is ever waxing, ever giving joy to the chakôra birds, shining *[Footnote 1]* This is one of the titles of the Mysore Râjas. *[Footnote 2]* In the repetitions of the grant both names occur. Holalkere Taluq

pion over those who say they are such and such,¹ subduer of the elephant army, son of Mali-Dêvi

made. And in order that *dharma* might be confirmed to that Vīra-Dêvarasa, he made grants of

ation. Usual final verses.

To Sirigiri .... châryya who did this work, the king, farmers and subjects, agreeing together,
made a grant for ever of 8 *kolaga*. Imprecation.

*Date 1515 A.D.*

(On the date specified),—in order that merit might accrue to Krishna-Râya-mahârâja,—for
the chatra of the god Mallikârjuna, Muluvâgil Mallinâtharasa's (or Nâgarasa's)² son Bâgûr Malla-
rasa granted the village of Âlahalli. (The grant is repeated). Usual final verses.

*Date 1226 A.D.*

Obeisances to S'ambhu &c. Be it well. When, (with usual titles), Hoysala vîra-Nârasimha-
Dêva, protecting the Gangavâdi Ninety-six Thousand and the Noḷambavâdi Thrity-two Thousand,
was in the residence of Dôrasamudra, ruling the kingdom in peace and wisdom :—(On the date
specified), the 9th year from his assuming the crown, the year Pârtthiva &c.,—certain gauḍas
(named) of Maṇali, which is Kêśavapura, fighting with various persons (named) of Hati and Santeya-
suri, died,—and the celestial nymphs bore them away in flowery cars to the highest *svarga*,
showing them the city of Kailâsa and the feet of Mahêsvara, and seating them on the thrones of
heroes. And on account of the departure (or death) of Mâdi-gauḍa, certain gauḍas (named) granted
*umbali* for the god Kali, for the sake of a *bîraga-liṁga*.

*Date 1237 A.D.*

Obeisance to S'ambhu &c. Be it well. When the pratâpa-cakravartti Hoysala vîra-Sômêsvara-
Dêvarasa was ruling the kingdom in peace :—(on the date specified), when Mâvinahaḷḷi Mâdaya and
.... yahalli Maleya-Nâyaka carried off the cows, Jaka-bôva (fought) and gained the world of *svarga*.
Mâra-bôva set up this stone for him.

*Date 1533 A.D.*

cells.remarks: by day as well as by night, hateful to the lotuses (the evil). Swifter than thought or the wind are his horsemen, the trampling of whose hoofs turns the world to clouds of dust,—why mention the slow-paced horses of Indra? Fanned with chāmaras by groups of the wives of hostile kings imprison- ed by him, distinguished as rājādhirāja, the terror of foreign kings, and by many other titles; often had he made the sixteen kinds of gifts in Gôkarṇa, Saṅgama, Nivṛtti, Suvarṇā, S’aṅkhādri, Parvata, Virinchipura and Kānchī, in the city of Kālahasti also, and in Kumbhakōṇa.<sup>1</sup> The ocean is drunk up by the clouds, it was swallowed by Agastya, it was agitated by the arrow of Rāghava, and is ever consumed by the flames of the submarine fire : it is indeed always in process of drying up, but the ocean of his bounty is always full. By Aṅga, Vaṅga, Kaliṅga and other foreign kings is he thus unceasingly addressed,—‘Victory ! Long life !’ Supreme is this king Achyuta, established on the jewel-throne, dwelling in Vijayanagara, rejoicing in the fullness of fame, excelling Nriga Nala Nahusha and other inferior kings, the home of unequalled valour and generosity. (On the date specified), on the bank of the Tungabhadrā river, in the presence of the (god) Viṭhalēśvara, he gave to Brahmans of many śākhās, gōtras, and sūtras, learned in the vēdas and śāstras, the Kēdagere village, (boundary villages named), a hamlet of Imāmbikasamudra in the the Nirugunda-śīma, attached to Yakkaṭi in the Hoysalạ kingdom, with all usual rights and details. On the application of one devoted to his master's service, having acquired the rules of policy, ...than the sun, distinguished for his agreeable speech, Timma-Nāyaka's son, versed in the hidden meanings of dharmma, a chintāmaṇi born from the ocean Timma-Nāyaka,—Hadapa Baiyapēndra, supporter of the performers of penance, who approached him with folded hands,—the king Achyuta-mahārāya, surrounded by priests and learned men, with all due ceremonies made the grant. The village was formed into 34 shares, the names of the recipients of which are here written. (Here follow the names and other details of the Brahmans). This śāsana of the king Achyuta was, by order, composed with soft expressions, by Sabhā- pati,—and engraved by Mallāṇa's son, the carpenter Vīraṇāchārya. Usual final verses. (signed)—śrī-Virūpāksha. Date 962 A.D. (On the date specified), Kāduvaṭṭi, Jagatunga-gāvunḍa's younger brother, fought and gained the world of gods. Date 1307 A.D. <kannada> ಅಂ. Obeisance to S'ambhu &c. Usual account of the origin and genealogy of the Hoy- </kannada> salas, down to Ballāla (III). Be it well. When, (with usual titles, including) Adiyama's Yama, gold (*kānchana*) to Kānchī (or the zone) ... ... ... , establisher of Chōla-Rāya, setter up of Pāṇḍya-Rāya, uprooter of Magara- Rāya, born in the Chālukya-kula,—Hoysaṇa vīra-Ballāla-Dēvarasa and Mādigi-Dēva-daṇṇāyaka were in the residence of Dōrasamudra, ruling the kingdom in peace and wisdom :— Be it well. When, possessed of the usual ascetic virtues (named); devoted to the worship of *aupāsana, agnihōtra*, the twice born, gurus and gods ; of a fame glorious as the sun ; daily performers of the six rites (named); shining lights in the qualities gained by the study of the Ṛig, Yajus, Sāma and Atharbbana vēdas, and the vēdānta ;-the hundred and twenty Brahmans of the all-worshipful great agrahāra Udbhava-Sōmanāthapura, which was Nirugunda, were ruling the kingdom in peace and wisdom :- Footnote 1. For these places see No. 94 above.

cells.remarks: Holalkere Taluq In the Gangavadi Ninety-six Thousand, in the Arabala Seventy, the first place was Honneya- kere.—To describe the fame and greatness of its gaudas ;—Praise of Sôma-gavuda, called Abhinô- malla. To him and his wife Lakha-gavudi was born Malli-gavuda. (On the date specified), he made a grant of lands (specified) for the god Prasanna-Mallinâtha, with certain grants of oil from the oil- mills. Usual final verses. This śâsana of the god Prasanna-Mallinâtha was written (i. e. engraved) by âchâri Êchôja's son Sidôja Sômôja. Date 1307 A.D. (On the date specified),—praised by all the world ; having gained five hundred vira-śâsanas ; adorned with many good qualities, truth, purity, good character, respect, humility and intelligence ; embodiments of heroes ; protectors of the Vira-Bananju-dharmma, the Setti-guttas of the Arabala Seventy, the paṭṭana-svâmi, temple priests and all the eighteen castes gave a śâsana as follows :— To Mâra-gavuda of Honneyakere we give the office of nâd-heggade, with one pana from each of 40 villages, half a pana from each of 30 villages, and the tolls, etcetera, of the fair. In confirmation of of this, the own signature of the nâd, —śrī-Gavarêśvara. The heggade Mâra-gavuda will provide 1 pa worth of oil every year for the 'light on the dîpa- mâla' of the god Prasanna-Mallinâtha.

text.remarks:
Obeisance to Ganâdhipati and to Sadâśiva

  Be it well. (On the date specified), several gaudas (named) of Jâjûru-sthala, with the approval
of their wives, sons and claimants, granted to Guruvanna, son of Halattihâla Basavappa-pûjâri of
the pancha-maṭha ...... the two villages Jâjûru and Kôtehâla, bought for 200 ga., with the usual
rights. Witnesses.Read more (1 KB)

38 Dâvanagere Taluq.
Given with libations of water, the boundary of that same pair of tanks is thus (34 lines following contain details of boundaries) -- thus the four boundaries of that pair of tanks are to be protected by you, future [rulers] born in our lineage or by other kings. And thus it has been said by the holy Vēdabāyēsēna:
Land has been given by many kings, beginning with Sagara; whoever at any time holds the earth, to him belongs the reward at that time.
And the sin of taking it away has also been declared by him:
Whosoever takes away land given by himself or by another, he is born as a worm in excrement for sixty thousand years.
He who takes away even a single piece of gold, a single cow, or even a single angula of land, attains hell until the final dissolution of creation.
In waterless forests of the Vindhyas, in dry tree-hollows... black serpents are born...
And Râmabhadra says...
This general bridge of dharma for kings is to be protected by you from time to time; Râmabhadra begs again and again all these future great kings:
Whether born in my lineage or in the lineage of other kings, those future kings on earth whose minds are free from sin, who protect this entire dharma of mine -- to them an âñjali is respectfully raised by me upon my head.

Mangala, great fortune.

taking it away has also been declared by him:Whosoever takes away land given by himself or by another, he is born as a worm in excrement for sixty thousand years.He who takes away even a single piece of gold, a single cow, or even a single angula of land, attains hell until the final dissolution of creation.In waterless forests of the Vindhyas, in dry tree-hollows... black serpents are born...And Râmabhadra says...This general bridge of dharma for kings is to be protected by you from time to time; Râmabhadra begs again and again all these future great kings:Whether born in my lineage or in the lineage of other kings, those future kings on earth whose minds are free from sin, who protect this entire dharma of mine -- to them an âñjali is respectfully raised by me upon my head.Mangala, great text.text_original: ದಾವಣಗೆರೆಯ ಮುಸಾಫಿರ ಬಂಗೆಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬಿದಿ ರುವ ಕಲ್ಲುಪ್ರಮಾಣ 7' 9"x1' 5"22ವಾದಿಮೂವತ್ತಿ ಚಾ ಸನಸಿರೆಮುಮಂಸ ಕ್ಮ ಛಿಗೆ ಮಂದುಷ್ಕನಿಗ)ಹತಿಸ್ಟೃಪ)ತಿಐಾ ಳನದಿಂಬೆಲ್ಫು ಯುವಿ23ಸಚ`ನನೆಲೆವೀಡಿನೊಳುಸ ಸುಖಸಂಕತಾ ವಿನೋದದಿಂರಾ ಮಿರಠೆ | ತತ್ಕಾ ದಪದೊ ಸ್ಮ್ಪೀಪಜೀನಿ | ಸ್ಪ ಸ್ಫಸ್ತಿ ತ್ರೀ24ಮಹಿಮಾಸ್ಪದಂಪತಿನ ದಾಬಾ ರಾಥಕಂ ಸು ತ್ಯಂಚಲದಂಕರಾಮನಭಯಂಗಂಭೀರರಾನ್ತ. ಘರೆಂ25ಸೂ ರೀಥ್ಭೃತಮಸ ಷಂ ಹಿತವ್ಯಾ ನಾರ . ವಿಸ್ನಾರೋಜ್ಟಿ ನತಭಾಸುರೋರ್ಜಿತೆಯಕಂವೈರೀಭ26ಸ6ಕಡ6ರವಂ | ನುಡಿದುದೆವನ್ನಿ ಮಾಡಿದುದೆ 699 999 * ೨9 ಸಾ27 ಡಾತ ಸ್ಗದೆ ಬನ್ನುದೆಭಾಸುರಕೀಡ್ರ್ರ್ಯ೯ ವಲ್ಚಿ28ವೆ ನೋಲ್ಯೇ ನಾಯಕಂ ಆ ಇದಳು ಜ %29ಸನ ಯತವಂತನಗೆ ರತಾ30೯ಭರಣಂಸಕಳಧೆರ್ಮ ಸಮುದ್ದರೆ ಹರಸು ಜನವಿನೋದಂಕೋದಣ್ಣಾ31॥ರಾಮಂಚಲದಂಕರಾಮಂಪವಾಣ ನಿದ್ದೇವನಾದಾಬ್ಯ ಭಿ)ಗಂಸಾಹಸೋತ್ತು,ಂಗಂತೆವ್ಯಾ ಡರುಕ್ಸಣಂಗ್‌32ಡಕುಜುಂಗುಡಿಯಾಳ್ಯವರಿಚ್ಟೇದಿಗಣ್ಣ ಪಲ್ಲವರಾಯಪಡೆವಡಿನೊಳುತಾಂಮಾಡಿಸಿದರಾಯ33ರಾಜಬಣ ಊೂರಾಳ್ವಕ್ರವಾಸುದೇವಗ್ಗೆ ನಿತ್ಯನಿವೇದ್ಯಾಂಗಭೋಗಕ್ಕಂಖಂಡಜ್ಬುಟ ಟತಜಣ್ನೊ ನೇದ್ಭಾ ರಕಠ್ಯಾಂ34ರದಾವಕ್ಕು ವಾಗಿಜೆಲು,ಯುಪನ್ನೆ ಸರಡಆಕೂಳಗಣಬೆಳ್ಳೋರತಾರಣವಳ್ಳಿ ಯುಮವನರಸನಕೆಆಯ35ಲಗ ದುಮುತ ತರುತೋಂಟದಲಿತ್ರಿಭೋಗಾ ೨ಭ್ಯ್ಯನ್ಮ ಇ 1. ಳು ಕ್ಯವಿಕ್ರ ಮವರ್ಷದಲಿ ೫ ನೆಯ36ಸೋಭಕ್ರು,ತುಸಂವತ್ಸರದುತ್ತ ರಾಯಣಸಂಕಾ)ನಿಯಮ್ಚರಾಯಶಾಣ್ಯ ಸ ಸದೇವರಕಯ್ಯಲುವ37ರಮೇಶ್ಶರದತ್ರಿ ಯಾಗೆ ಚಂದಾ)ರ್ಕ್ಯನತಾರಂಬರಂಸಲ್ಪಾಂತಾಗಿಪರಿಜ್ಚೇದಿನಾಯಕಂ ೦ಪಡೆದುದೇವರ್ಗ್ಗೆಕೊಟ್ಟ38ಈಸ್ರಾವಕ್ಕೆಸ್ಥಾನಪತಿಯಾಗಿಕ್ರೀಕೃೃಷ ಬಲ್ಲೆ ಸವಾನತಿರುಮಲೆನಂಬಿಗೆಪರಿಜೆ ಸದಿವಾ ಯಕಂಕೊಟ್ಟ |39ನ ೀಧಮ್ಮರಮನಾವನೋರ್ವ್ವಂಪ ದವತಳಿಸಿದಂಗುಗೆಯಬಾ ಉರಾಸಿಪ)ಯಾಗೆಕುರುಸ್ತೇತಾ)40೯ ತೀತ್ರ ೯ಂಗಳೊಳುಸಾಸಿರವ್ನದಶಾರಗರಪ್ಪಬಾ)ಹ ಊರ್ಗೆ ಸಾಸಿರಕವಿಲೆಯಕೋಡುಂ41ಕೊಳಗುಮಂಪೊೋನ್ನಿ ಂಪಂಚರತ್ಪ ದಿಂಕಟ್ಕ್ಯಸಿಸಂಕ್ರಾನಿ ಮ್ನ ತೀಪಾತಗ 1 /ಹಣಂಗಳೊಳುಕೊಟ್ಟ ಸಪ್ರಣ್ಯನ42ಛಮನೆಯ್ಲ್ಹುವರು| ಇನ್ನೀಧರ್ಮಮವಾವನೋವ್ನ್ಹ೯ನಳಿದವವಾತೀತ್ಯ ಇಂಗಳೊಳ್‌ಸಾಸಿರಬಾ ೨ )ಹ್ಹ್ರಣರುವುಂ43ಸಾಸಿರಕನಿಕೆಯುವುನಾತೀರ್ತ್ವಂಗಳೊಳಳಿದಮಹಾವಾತಕನಕ್ಕುಸ್ಕದತ,೦44ಪರದತಂವಾಯೋಹರೇತುವಸುವ್ಹರಾ | ಸಷ್ಟಿರ್ವುರ್ಷಸಹಸ್ರಾಣಾಂವಿಷ್ಣ್ಯಾಯಾಂಜಾಯತೇಶ್ರಿಮಿ45ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯೋಯಂಥಮ ನಸೇತುರ್ನ್ಯ್ಯಪಾಣಾಂಕಾಲೇಕಾಲೇಶಾಲನೀಯೋಥವರದ್ಧಿ ಃಸವ್ಮಾ46ನೇತಾಮಭಾವಿವಪಂತ್ತಿ ೯ವೆಂದ್ರೋಭೋೊಯೋಭೂಯೋಯಾಚತೇರಾಮಭದ್ರ)॥47ವವಿಸಂವಿಸಮಿತ್ಯಾಹೂದೇವಸ್ಥವಿ ಸಮುಜ್ಯತೇನಿಷಮೇಕಾಕಿನಂಹನಿ48ದೇವಸ್ಟೈಂಪುತನೌತ್ರಿ)ಕಂ ॥ ಕವಿಮಾದಿರಾಜಬರದಂಕಡಬಾಚಾಠಿಕಂಡರಿಸಿದಂ।

ôṁ namas Si'vâya

namas tuṅga &c. ||
viśuddha-jñâna-dêhâya tri-vêdi-divya-chakshushê |
śrêyaḥ-prâpti-nimittâya mâmas Sômârdha-dhâriṇê ||
pratyaksha-vastu-viṣayâya jagadd-hitâya
viśva-sthiti-pralaya-sambhava-kâraṇâya |
sarvvatmanê vijita-kôpa-manôbhavâya
tubhyam namas tri-bhuvana-prabhavê S'vâya ||
śrî-vallabhan ahita-jaya- | śrī-vallabhan udadhi-parivṛitâkhila-dhâtri- |
śrî-vallabhan amala-yaśas- | śrî-vallabha chakravartti Vikrama-bhûpam ||


Om! Salutation to Śiva!

Salutation to Tuṅga &c. ||
To Him whose body is pure knowledge, who possesses the three Vedas as divine eyes, whose purpose is the attainment of welfare, who wears the crescent moon [Sômârdha-dhâriṇê]; to Him who is the perceptible object, who is for the benefit of the world, who is the cause of the preservation, destruction, and creation of the universe; to the Universal Soul, who has conquered anger and passion (Kôpa-manôbhava), to Thee, the Lord (S'vâya) who is the origin of the three worlds, salutation!
Śrî-vallabha, conqueror of enemies; Śrî-vallabha, [lord of] the entire earth girt by the ocean; Śrî-vallabha of stainless fame; Śrî-vallabha, the emperor Vikrama-bhûpa ||

Dâvaṇagere Taluq.

svasti samasta-bhuvanāśrayam śrī-pṛthivi-vallabha mahārājādhirāja paramēśvara parama-bhaṭṭārakaṁ
Satyāśraya-kula-tilakam Chālukyābharaṇam śrīmat-Tribhuvanamalla-Dēvara vijaya-rājyam uttarōtta-
rābhivṛddhi-pravarddhamānam ā-chandrārkka-tāram-baram saluttam ire || tat-pāda-padmōpajīvi sama-
dhigata-pañcha-mahā-śabda mahā-sāmantādhipati mahā-prachaṇḍa-daṇḍanāyaka bēḍida-vara-dāyaka
su-jana-prasanna nuṇḍidu-matt-enna gōtra-pavitra parāṅganā-putra .... ya-Rēvanta vairi-Kritānta
sāhasōttuṅgan ayyana nāmādi-samasta-prasti-sahita śrīman-mahā-pradhānam Bāṇasa-
vergge-daṇ luyākan Anantapālayyaṅgaḷa besadim samasta-rājya-bhara-nirūpita-mahāmātya-pada-
vi-virājamāna mānōnnata prabhu-mantrōtsāha-śakti-traya-sampannam nuṇḍidu-matt-enna gōtra-pavitra
parāṅganā-putran ayyana sāmâdi-samasta-praśasti-sahitam śrīmad-achchhu-pannâyad.adhishṭā-
yaka śrīmatu Bammarasaru Noḷambavāḍi-mūvatt-irchchhhāsirada pannāyamam dushṭa-nigraha-
visishta-pratipālanadim sukhadin āluttam ire ||

svasti samasta-vastu-guṇa-bhūshaṇan ūjjijita-tējan ātma-vam- |
sa-stutan ishta-sishta-phala-dāyakan Īśa-padābja-sambhṛtō- |
nmastakan aṅganā-jana-virājita-pina-payōdharārppitō- |
ras-sthalaṇ aty-udara-charitam vibhu-Bammarasam dharitriyol ||
Kōṅgaḷi-nāḍol aggada-Kadambaḷi-sāyirad-āgaraṅgaloḷ |
dēgulakam Jiṇālayakav āravegam kere-bāvi-satrakam |
rāgade tanna pannayada suṅka-doḷam daśa-pannav ittan int |
āgaram uḷḷinam negarda-Bammarasam guṇa-ratnad-āgaram ||
piridum sad-bhaktiyim Beḷṭuruvada Giri-râjātmajēśange Sarppē- |
śvara-dēvaṅga aṅga-bhōgārchchanege sale nivēdya-pradipakkani oḷpim |
dharaṇam tingalge paryyāyadoḷe salisuvan ant āgiral mādidam Ba- |
mmarasam pannāyadoḷ Dharmmamāman ina-śasiy-uḷḷannam utsāhadindam ||

Châlukya-Vikrama-kâlada 33 neya Sarvvadhâri-saṁvatsarada Pushya-śuddha-pañchami-Bihavârad-
and uttarâyaṇa-saṁkramaṇa-vyatipita-nimittun âgi Nilaṇṭha-paṇḍitara kâlam karchchi dhârâ-
pûrvvakam mâḍi śri-Sarppêśvara-dêvar-aṅga-bhôga-pradipa-nivêdyakkam endu Bammarasam tanna
paṇannâyada suṁkaḍoḷu tiṅgaḷingu aydu-paṇamam Paramêśvara-dattiy âgi biṭṭu-koṭṭan int î-dharmmaman
âr orvvar pratipâlisidavargge Vârâṇasi-Kurukshêtrâṅgyatîrtthadoḷu sahasra-vêda-pâragar appa
brâhmaṇargge sahasra-kavileya koḍum koḷagumam pañcha-ratnaṅgaḷim kaṭṭisi-koṭṭa phalam akku
î-dharmmaman aḷidavar anibar-brâhmaṇaraman aṇitu-kavileyuman â-tîrtthangalol aḷida pâtakan
akku ‖ (usual final verse) svasti ‖

ಸಸ್ಸಿ ಸಹಿ11ತಾಂತ್ರಿಮನ್ಮ ಹಾಪ)ಧಾನಂಬಾಣಸವೆಗ್ಗ ನಡೆದಲ್ನಾ ನಾಯಕನನನ ಪಾಳಯ್ಯ್ಯಂ12ಗಳಬೆಸೆನಿಂಸಮಸ | ರಾಜ್ಯಭರನಿರೂಪಿತಮಹಾಮಾತ್ಯಪದನೀನಿ13ರಾಜಮಾನವೊನೋನ್ನ ತಪ ಲ. ತ್ತಾ ಬ್ರಹಶಕ್ತಿತ್ರ)ಯಸಾಹ14ಸಮುಡಿದುಮತ್ತೆನ್ನ ಗೋಡತ್ರ)ನ ಪರಾಂಗ ನಾಪುತ)ನಯ್ಯ್ಯನಸಿಂ15ಗವಮಾದಿಸಮಸ್ತಪ್ರ) ಸಸ್ತಿ, ಸಹಿತ ಶ್ರೀಮದಚ್ಚು ಪನ್ನ್ವಾಯ16ದಧಿಸಾಸ್ರ್ಯಕ್ರೀಮತುಬವ್ಮು ರೆಸರುನೊಳಂಬವಾಡಿಮೂ17ವತ್ರಿಚ್ಚಾ ಇಸಿರದಪೆನ್ನಾಯಮಂದುಷ ನಿಗ್ರ) ಹನಿಸಿಸ್ಟೃಪ್ರತಿ18ಪಾಲನಸುಖವಿಧಿವಾಳುತ್ತ ದಿರೆ॥ ಸ್ಪಸ್ತಿ ಸಮಸ್ತವಸ್ತು ಗುಣಭೂಷ19ಣವೊಜ್ವಿ ಇಶತತೇಜನಾತ್ವವಂಸಸ್ಳು ತನಿಷ್ಟ್ಯ ಶಿದೆ ಫಲದಾಯಕನೀಕಪದಾಬ್ಯ ಶಂ20ಪ್ರೆತೋನ್ಯ ಶ್ರಕನುಗನಂಜನನಿರಾಜಿತಪ್ಪಾನನಯೋಧರಾಜ್ಚಿ ೯ತೋರಸ್ಮಳನತ್ಯು21ದಾರಚರಿತಂವಿಭುಬಮ್ಮ ರಸಂಧರಿತ್ರಿಯೊಳ್‌ ॥ ಕೊಂದಲಿನಾಡೊಳಗ್ಗ ದಕದಂಬ22ಳಿ ಸಾಯಿರದಾಗರಂಗಳೊಳ್‌ ದೇಗುಲಕಂಜಿನಾಲಯಕವಾರವೆಗಂಕೆ ಆ್‌ದಾವಣಗೆರೆ ತಾಲೂಕು 67೨೩ಬಾವಿಸತ) ಕಂರಾ ದೆತನ್ನ ಪನ್ನೆಯದಸುಂಕದೊಳ೦ದಶವನ್ನ ವಿತ್ತನಿನ್ನಾಗರವು೨೪ನಂನೆಗದ್ದಬಮ್ಮ ರಸಂಗುಣರತ್ಸ್ವದಾಗರಂ | ಪಿರಿದು೦ಸದ್ದತ,ಯಿಂಬೆಲ್ಮುಟಿ೨೫ವದಗಿರಿರಾಜಾತ್ಮ ಜೇಶಂಗೆ ಸಸ್ಪೆನೇಶ್ಶರದೇವಂಗಂಗಭೋಗಾರ್ಚ್ವನೆಗಸಲೆನಿ೨೬ವೈದ್ಯಪ್ರದೀಪಕ್ಕಮೊಳ್ಳಿಂಧರಣೀತಿಂಗಳ್ಳೆ ಪಯ್ಯಾಕಯದೊಳೆಸಲಿಸುವ೨೭ನ್ಹಾಗಿರಲ್ಮಾಡಿದಂಬಮ್ಮರಸಂಪನ್ಮಾಯದೊಳ್‌ಧರ್ಮ್ಮಮನಿನಶಕಿಯುಳ್ಳನ್ನ ಮು ೨೮೨೯ತಳ್ಸ್ಪಹದಿಂದಂ | ಚಾಳುಕ್ಯುವಿಕ್‌ /ಮಕಾಲದ ೩೩ ನೆಯಸರ್ವ್ವಧಾರಿಸಂ೩೦ವತ್ಸರದಫು ಕ್ಯಾಕುದ್ಧ ಪಂಚಮಿಬಿ)ಹವಾರದಂದುತ್ತ ರಾ ಉಯಣಾಸಂಕ)ಮಣವ್ಯತೀವಾತನಿಮಿತ್ರಮಾಗಿನೀ೩೧ಲಕಂಠನಂಡಿತರಕಾಲಕಜ್ಚ್ವಿ೯ಧಾ ರಾಪೂರ್ವ್ಮ ಕಂಮಾಡಿ೩೨ (ಸಸ್ಟೆ ಸರಶರದೇವೆರಂಗಭೋಗವ)ದೀಪನಿವೇದ್ಯಕ್ಕಂ೩೩ಮಂದುಬಮ್ಮರಸಂತನ್ನ ಬುಬಾ)ಹ್ಮಣರ್ಗ್ಗಸಹಸ್ರ)ಕವಿಲೆ೩೭ಯಕೋಡುಂಕೊಳುಗುಮಂಪಂಚರತ್ನಗಳಿಂಕಟ್ಟಿ ಸಿ೩೮ಕ್ಷೂಟ್ಮಫಲಮಕ್ಕುಈಧರ್ಮ್ಮಮನಳಿದವರನಿಬಬ್ಬಾ೩೯ಟ್‌ ೪೦೫ ಉರುಮನನಿತುಕವಿಲೆಯುಮನಾತೀರ್ತ್ಥ್ಯಂಗಳೊಳಳಿ೪೧ದರಾತಕನಕ್ಕು ! ಸ್ಪುದತ್ತಂಪರದತ್ತೈ text.text_original: ಹರಿಹರದಲ್ಲಿ ಹರಿಹರೇಶ್ವರ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನದ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಕಡೆ ನೆಟ್ಟಿರುವ ಕಲ್ಲುಪ್ರಮಾಣ 5' × 2'1 ಶ್ರೀಹರಿಹರಾಯನಮಃ ನಮಂಗತಿರಶೃಂಬಿಚಂದ ಚಾಮರಚಾರವೇತ್ರೈತ್ತ್ರ ಲೋಕ್ಯ2 ನಗರಾರಂಭಮೂಲಸ್ತಂಭಾಯಕಂಭವೇಶಿಗೌರೀವಿಲಸದ್ದಾ ಹುವಲ್ಲೀವೇಲ್ಲಿತವಿಗ್ರಹಂ3 ಮದ್ದೇಹರಿಸರಾಕಾರಾನಲ್ಬಕಲ್ಪಮಹೀರುಹಂ | ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿಶಿಜಯಾಭ್ಯುದಯಶಾಲಿವಾಹನ4 ಶಕವರ್ಷ ೧೮೩೩ ನೆಯಅನಂದಸಂವತ್ಸರದವಮಯಿಶಾಖಶು ೧೫ ಸೋಮವಾರನಲುಕಿ ಮ5 ವ್ತ್ರ ಹಾರಾಇಜಾಧಿರಾಜರಾಜಪರಮೇಶ್ವರಕ ಫವೀರಥ ತಾಪಸದಾಶಿವಪದೇವಮಹಾರಾಯ6 ರುವಿದ್ಯಾನಗರಿಯಲ್ಲೂಸುಮುಸೆಸುಕಥಾನಿನೋದಿದುಸಿಹ್ವಾಸನಾರೂಢಾಗಿವುಧೀ ದಲ್ಲಿ7 ರಾಜ್ಯಂಗೆಯಿಉತ್ತಿ ಪ್ರಸುರಸಮಯದಲುಸ್ಸಾಸ್ಟಿ ುಸ ಸ.ಭುವನಾಧೀಶ್ಚರದೇವಾಧಿದೇವಂದೇವನರ8 ಮೇಶ್ಚರಕ್ಕೆ ವವೈಸ ಸ ಇನಿಜೇದವಾದವಿದ್ದೇಂಸನಮಾರ್ಕಂಡೇಯವರಪ್ರದಾನಕಾರಣಹರಿಹರೈಕ್ಯಾವ9 ತಾರಗುಹಾಸುರವುದವಿದಾರಣಾಗುಹಾ ಸುರವಕ್ಷೋನಿತ್ರಿಪ್ರಚರಣಾರವಿಂದಯುಗಃ ಸ್ಮ10 ಲ್ಲಿ ೧೦೭೧ ರಮರ್ತ್ಯಪಾತಾಳತ್ರಿಭುವನಪೂಜಿತಭಕ್ಕ ಜನದಭೀಷ್ಮ್ಯಾಥಾಸಿದ್ಧಿ ದಾಯಕಗುಹಾರಣ್ಯವೆಂಬ11 ಪುಣ್ಯಾರಣ್ಯಾನಿವಾಸಿಗಳ್ಗೆ ನವರೆತಅಭಯದಾನಮಂಮಾಳ ಸತುಂಗಭದಾ ಪೂರ್ವ ಕೂಲನಿ12 ವಾಸನೆನಿಸಿದಕೂಡಲೂರಪುರವರಾ ಧೀಶ್ಯರನಾದಶಿ ಪ್ರ) ಸಂನಹರಿಸರದೇವರಿಗೆಆಸದಾತಿ.13 ದೇವಮಹ ರಾಯರಹಡಪದಸಿಂಧುಗೋವಿಂದಶಿತಕರಗಂಡಧವಳಾಂಕಛೀಮಮಣಿನಾಗ14 ಪ್ರರವರಾಧೀಶ್ವರ ಯಪ್ಪನಾಯಕರಮಕಳುಕ್ರುಹಪ್ಪವಾಯಕರುಕಿ ನರಸಿಹ ನಂ15 ಪುಣ್ಯಕಾಲದಲುತಂಮತಂದೆಬ್ಬೇಯಸ್ಸನಾಯಕರಿಗೂತಂಮತಾಯಿಕೊಂಡ16 ವಮಂಮ ನವರಿಗೂಪುಂಣ್ಯವಾಗಬೇಕೆಂದುಬೆಳುವಡಿಯಗ್ರಾಮವನೂಶಿ)ಹರಿಹರದೇವರ17 ಮಧ್ಯನ್ಯಂನದವ ತ)ಕೆಸಮರ್ಪ್ಪಿಸಿಐಕಾಂತದವಸರದಅತಿರಸದನೈವೇದ್ಯಕ್ಕೆಹರಿಹರ18 ದ . . . . ತನೆಯ . . . ಸಮಪಿ ೯ಸಿಅತಿರಸವನೂಸ್ಫಾಮಿಗೆನೈವೇದ್ಯು19 ದಸಮರ್ಪ್ಪಣೆಗೆಟೆಳ್ಳಿಯಹರಿವಾಣವನೂಸಮ ಖ್ಬುಸಿಕುತಾರ್ಥನಾದನುಖಾಧರ್ಮವನುಪ್ರ)20 ತ್ರಿವಾಲಿಸುವಂಥಾವರಿಗೆಅನಂತಅಶ ಇಮೇಧಯಾಗದಲವಹುದುಯಾಧಮರವನೂಉ21 ಜ್ಜೀದಿಸದೆಅಳಿದರಣಪಿಷ ಟಗಂಗೆಯಲೂಗೋಬಾ)ಹ ಉಮಾತಾಪಿತ್ರುಗಳವಧೆಯಮಾ22 ಡಿಮಾತ್ರುಗಮನಪುತ /ಮಾಂಸವನೂಭತಕ್ಷಿಸಿದಲರಾಪವಹುದುವಿಂದುಬರದಕಿಲಾಕ್ತ್‌23 ರ || ಸ್ನದತಾ ದ್ವೀಗುಣ೦ಪುಂಕ್ಳಾ೦ಪರದತಾ ನುಪಾಲನಂಪರದತಾ ಪಹಾರೇಣಸ್ಕದತ ಂನಿಃಫಲಂಭೆ24 ವೇತೃ | ದಾನರಾಖನಯೋರ್ಮೈಥ್ಯೆ ೀದಾವಾಛೆೇಯೋನುವಾಲನಂದಾವಾತ ಸ ನಮವಾಸ್ನೋತಿನಿಪಾಲ25 ನಾಮಚ್ಛು ತೆಂಪದಂ || . . . . . . . . . . . ಳ್ಳಿಯಗ್ರಾಮವನುಶಿ)ಹರಿಹರದೇವರಥರ ್ಮ26 ವೃತ್ತಕೆ . . . . . . . . . . ಕಾಮರಸಮಕ್ಕಳಿದಾನವಪ್ಪೆಗಮಂಗಳಮ27 ಹಾ ಶ್ರೀ ಶ್ರೀ

svasti śrî jayâbhuyudaya-S'âlivâhana-śaka-varsha 1452 Vikṛuti-samvatsarama S'râvaṇa-bahula 8 yu Sôma-vâra-jayantî-puṇya-kâladalli śrî-Kṛiṣhṇâvatâra-samayadalli śrîmad-râjâdhirâja râja-paramêśvara śrî-vîra-pratâpa-Achyuta-Râya-mahârâyaru sukha-saṅkathâ-vinôdadim pṛthvî-râjyam geyutti iralâgi svâmi namage Amara-nâyakatanakke palisida Koṭṭūra-châvaḍige saluva Uchchaṅgi vênṭheyad olaqaṇa Pâṇḍya-nâḍige saluva Hariharada simeya volaqaṇa Achyutarâyapurapuram endu prati-nâmadhêyav âda Buḷḷâpuram emba grâmavanu Vasisḥṭha-gôtrada Âśvalâyana-sûtrada chinna-bhaṇḍârada Timm-arasara makkalu Nârâyaṇa-Dêvagalu śrî-Harihara-dêvara avasara-satrakke samarppisiddu eraḍu-pâlu Gautama-gôtrada Âśvalâyana-sûtrada Hariharada Râmachandrârâdhyara makkalu Viśvêśvarârâdhyarige śrî-Harihara-dêvara sannidhiyalli sa-hiraṇyôdaka-dâna-dhârâ-pûrvvakav âgi koṭṭadu vondu-pâlu yî-rîtiya tri-bhâgadalli nimma putra-pautra-paramparayâgi â-chandrâra-sthâyigaḷ âgi sukhadim anubhavisuviri yandu koṭṭa-dharma-śâsana || (usual final verses)

gṛhṇanti yâvataḥ pâmsum rudatam aśri-bindavaḥ |

dDaitya-balam ati-samuddhatam Trairājya-Pallava-balam avashtabhya(h) samasta-vishaya-praśa-

evam ājñāpayati viditam astu vō'smābhi[h] shoḍaśōttara-shachchhatēshu S'aka-varshēshv atitēshu
pravarddhamāna-vijaya-rājya-samvatsarē chaturddaśē varttamānē Harishapura-pratyāsannē Ka-
rañjapatra-grāmam adhivasati vijaya-skandhāvārē Kārttikē paurṇamāsyām śrimad-Āluva-Rāja-
vijñāpanayā Vātsyasa-gōtrasya S'ri-sarmmaṇaḥ sōmayājinaḥ putrāya Mâra-sarmmaṇaḥ putrāya Isâna
śarmmaṇē vēda-vēdāṅga-pārāgayā Vanavāsi-maṇḍalē Edēvoḷal-bhāge Kiṟu-Kāmbāsi-nāmâ grāma-

tram cha tasya kṣhētrasya sīmā pūrvvôttara-dig-bhāgē Sirigâlu-grāma-sīmī Pulivutu tata âgatya |
Kavvesurigolam | tataḥ Perbbuttu | tata (III a) Âldore | tatah Aḷgoḷa | tatô Nittakoḷa tatah prâg
gatvā Nēṟiḷgere | tatah Kurupakere | tatah dakshiṇa-diśam āvṛitya Arakattaṇat tad âgāmbihir asmad-
vamsyai[r a]nyaiś cha rājabhir āyur-aiśvaryâdinâm vilasitam achirâṁśu-chañchalam avagachchhâd-
bhir â-chandra-dharaṇṇava-sthiti-sama-kâḷam yaśaḥ chhichshubhis sva-datti-nirvvissēsham paripâla-
nīyam uktañ cha bhagavatā vēda-vyâsēna Vyâsēna

೨ನ್‌ಮಗಾವುಣ್ಯ ಸನಸನ್ನಿಧಾನವಲುಯಮನಿಯಮಸ್ಸಾಧಾಯಧನ್ಯಾನಧಾರಣಮೋವನಾಮಷ್ಠಾ
೨೧೧ಜನಸಮಾಧಿಕೀಳಸುಪನ್ನೆ ರಪ ಶ್ರೀಮತುಕಾಕಂಬಾಳನ್ಬೈಸ್ಟಿ ಕತಫೋಧನರ,
೨೨ಚಿತಿ ಸ್ವರಪ್ನುಬಾಳಡೆಂದ ಪಂಡಿತರಕಾಲಂಕಷಿ ನಧಾರಾಭೂರ್ವ್ವ್ಯಕಂಮಾಡಿಕಡಲಬಾ
೨೩ಛಮೂಲಸ್ತಾನ ಲಿದೇವಸ್ನಾಮಿಯಲಗಭೋಗಕ್ಕಂಯಲ್ಲಿತಳಭಣ ದಸೆರ್ಜ್ಲ್ಲಂ೦
೨೪ಕದದಸವಂದಮಂಬಿಟ್ಟರುಯಿನ್‌ಧರ್ಮಮನಾರೊಪ್ನರುಪ್ಪು)ತಿಚಾಲಿಸಿ

ದಾವಣಗೆರೆ ತಾಲೂಕು
೨೬ದವತುಪಾ ೨ಯಾಗೆಬಾರಾಸಿಕುರುಕ್ಷೇತ್ರಅಗ ೫ತೀತ್ಯ ಇದಲುಸಾಸಿರ
೨೭ಕವಿಲೆಯಸಾಸಿರ್ವ್ವರುಬಾ ಣಗೆ ೯ಯುಭೆಯಮುಖಿದಾನಂಗೊಟ್ಟ ೈ
೨೮ಲಮನೆಯ್ಲುವರುಯಿನ್ಲೀಧಮ್ಮರಮನಾರೊಬ್ಬ ರಳಿದವರುದಿವ್ಯುತೀತ ನದಲುಸಾಸಿರ
೨೯ಪ್ರೋಧನರುಮಂಸಾಸಿರಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮ ರುಮಂಸಾಸಿರಕವಿಲೆಯುಪವನಳಿದವಾತಕರು ॥

text.text_original: ಹೋಬಳಿ ಕಡಬಾಳು ಗ್ರಾಮದ ಸರ್ವನಂಬರು ೧೯ ನೇ ಜವಾನಿನಲ್ಲಿ ನೆಟ್ಟಿರುವ ಕಲ್ಲುಪ್ರಮಾಣ 5' x 2' 6"1 . . . . . . ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿಜಂದ್ರಚಾಮರಚಾರವೆತ್ರ . . . . . .2 . . ಮೂಲಸಂ ಭಾಯಸಂಭವೆ . . . . . . .3 . . . . . . . ಪೂರ್ವದೇಶಮವ . . . . . . .4 . . . . . . . ಸಮಸ್ತಭುವನಾಶ್ರಯಶ್ರೀಪ್ರಥ್ವೀವಲಭಮಹಾ . . . . .6 . . . . . ಮಲ್ಲ . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .14 ಚಮಹಾಸಕಬ್ಬಮಹಂಸಂಮನ . . . . . . . . .15 ಕದಿನಾನಾಧಕಂ . . . . . ಕಲ್ಪಭೂಜ . . . . .16 . . . . ಪ್ರೋದ್ಯನಿತನಿಕುರಂಬಕಬಂಧನ . . . ತಿಹಿತಂ . .17 ನೆಯಸತ್ಯರಾಧೆಯು ನಿಜಕುಳಸರಸಿಜಾಕರತರಣಿಕಿರಣಂಕೌಸ್ತುವಾ18 ಭರಣಂನಾಮಾದಿಸಮಸಪ್ರಶಸ್ತಿ ಸಹಿತಂ ಶ್ರೀಮನ್ಯಹಾಸಾಮನ . . .19 ರುಚಾಳುಕ ಏಕಕ್ರಮವಸ ರ್ಷದ ೫ ನೆಯಪ್ರಥಮಾದಿಸಂವತ್ಸರದ ಫಾಲ್ಗುಣಶುದ್ಧಮಾವಾಸ್ಯಾದಿನಾರದುತ್ತರಾಯಣಸುಕ್ರಾನ್ನಿ ಸುರ್ಯ್ಯಗ್ರಹಣನಿಮಿತ್ತ ಮಾಸಿಕ ಮನ್ನೆ ಸಹಾಪ್ರಭುಸಾ೨ನ್‌ಮಗಾವುಣ್ಯ ಸನಸನ್ನಿಧಾನವಲುಯಮನಿಯಮಸ್ಸಾಧಾಯಧನ್ಯಾನಧಾರಣಮೋವನಾಮಷ್ಠಾ೨೧೧ಜನಸಮಾಧಿಕೀಳಸುಪನ್ನೆ ರಪ ಶ್ರೀಮತುಕಾಕಂಬಾಳನ್ಬೈಸ್ಟಿ ಕತಫೋಧನರ,೨೨ಚಿತಿ ಸ್ವರಪ್ನುಬಾಳಡೆಂದ ಪಂಡಿತರಕಾಲಂಕಷಿ ನಧಾರಾಭೂರ್ವ್ವ್ಯಕಂಮಾಡಿಕಡಲಬಾ೨೩ಛಮೂಲಸ್ತಾನ ಲಿದೇವಸ್ನಾಮಿಯಲಗಭೋಗಕ್ಕಂಯಲ್ಲಿತಳಭಣ ದಸೆರ್ಜ್ಲ್ಲಂ೦೨೪ಕದದಸವಂದಮಂಬಿಟ್ಟರುಯಿನ್‌ಧರ್ಮಮನಾರೊಪ್ನರುಪ್ಪು)ತಿಚಾಲಿಸಿದಾವಣಗೆರೆ ತಾಲೂಕು೨೬ದವತುಪಾ ೨ಯಾಗೆಬಾರಾಸಿಕುರುಕ್ಷೇತ್ರಅಗ ೫ತೀತ್ಯ ಇದಲುಸಾಸಿರ೨೭ಕವಿಲೆಯಸಾಸಿರ್ವ್ವರುಬಾ ಣಗೆ ೯ಯುಭೆಯಮುಖಿದಾನಂಗೊಟ್ಟ ೈ೨೮ಲಮನೆಯ್ಲುವರುಯಿನ್ಲೀಧಮ್ಮರಮನಾರೊಬ್ಬ ರಳಿದವರುದಿವ್ಯುತೀತ ನದಲುಸಾಸಿರ೨೯ಪ್ರೋಧನರುಮಂಸಾಸಿರಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮ ರುಮಂಸಾಸಿರಕವಿಲೆಯುಪವನಳಿದವಾತಕರು ॥

^7ಂಮಗವುಂಡನಮಗಸೋವೆಗವುಡನೂಹರಿಪಗವುಂಡನೂಕೊಂಡಂಜಿಯದಾರಿಯ
^8ಲುಮಸಣಕವೆ ಸಯಕೆಯಿಂದವುಪಡುವಲುಮತ್ತ್ತ ರುಪೊಂದನುಕೊಟ್ಟೆ ಸುಧುದಥ್ಣೆಯವರುದ್ದು

text.text_original: ಅದೇ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನದೆ ಮುಂದೆ ನಟ್ಟ ೧ ನೇ ವೀರಕಲ್ಲುಪ್ರಮಾಣ – 6' x 2'1ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಸಮಸ್ತ ಪ್ರಶಸ್ತಿ ಸಹಿತಂ ಶ್ರೀಮನ್ಮಹಾಮಂಡಳೇಶ್ವರಂವಿಜಯವಾಣ್ಣದೇವರುವೊಇಂಬಮೂವತ್ತಿ ಚಾ2ಸಿರಮುಮಂಸುಖಸಂಕಥಾವಿನೋದದಿಂರಾಜ್ಯಂಗೆಯ್ದುತ್ತವಿರೆ॥ ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ, ಸಮಸ್ತ ಪ್ರಶಸ್ತಿ3ಸಹಿತಂ ಶ್ರೀಮನ್ಯಹಾಸಾಮಂತಂಲಕ್ಷ್ಮೀಮಣತುತ್ತಸಡನಿಲಾಡುಕೊಪ ಕ ಐಂ , ಬಅಸಿಡಿಲುಬಿಗಿದಪ್ಪುವಂ ಪ್ರನಾಮವನ್ತ್ವ4ಅಣ್ಣನಗಂಧವಾರಣಂಮಾ . . ಸ್ಥಿಸಹಿತಂಕ್ರೀಮನ್ಯಹಾಸಾಮಂತಂಲಕ್ಷ್ಮೀಮಣ ತುತ್ತಸಡನಿಲಾಡುಕೊಪ ಕ ಐಂ . . . ಅವನೊ5ಮದನಮಹೇಶ್ವರಂಅರಿಬಿರುವಸಾಮಂತರಶಿರವಜ್ರದಂಡಂಅಯ್ಯನೆ . . . ಚು6ಹಚ್ಚೆ ಗಂಡಂಕಟ್ಕಬಿಡುವಸಾಮಂತರಗಂಡುಮಂಡಳಿಕಸಾಮಂತತೀರ್ತ್ನದ . . ಳವಂಸಿಂ ಇ 32೫೩೭೨ ಸಸಾವಂತರನಿಟೆಲ್ಲಮುಅವಂವಿಾಜುವಸಾವಂನ ರದಿ7ಮುಳಸೂಸುವಂಗಡಿಯಂಕಭೀವ: ೦ಉಳನೀಶ್ಚರದೇವರಪಾದಾರಾಧಕಂಭು8ಬಬಳಸಾಧಕಂವಿನಾಯಕದೇವರಲಬ್ಬವರಪ್ರಸಾದಂಬಾಯಕುಳಿತಿಳಕಂಡಿಸ9ನದಸಾಮಂತಚಟ್ಟಯನಾಯಕನಮಗಸಾಮಂತಬೆನವಯನಾಯಕ10ಸಾವಂತಹುಣಿ . . . ಜಮುನ ಅ . . . . 6 . . . . ಹರಿಯಮನಾಯಕಮಂಜಿಸನಮುಮಂಕೊ11 . . . . . . . ಕ್ರೊಕುಲೂರುಮಂಹೊಗೆಯ . . ಯಂಸುಖಸಂಕಥಾವಿನೋದದಿಂ12 . . . . . . . ಸೂಳೆಯಕಾಳೆಯಮಗಹಡವಳಬೆ . . .13ರಾಜ್ಯಂಗೆಯ್ಯುತ ನುರೆಅನೂರ ರುನುಂಚಂಡೆಯಮಂಕೆಆಯನುಂಬಾಳನವಂಮಾಡಿನಾಲ್ದರುಸತ ಲಿಸೆಪ್ರ)14[ಭ]ವಸುವತ್ಸರದಮಾಘಬಹುಳ ೫ ಮಿಸೋಮವಾರದಂದುಶೀರಗಲಂನಿಅಸುವ15ಮುಗುಳಿಯಕೆಆೌಯಕೆಳಗೆಗದ್ದೆ ಈ ೧೦೦ ಶೆಂಕಣಹೊಲದಹ . ಕೆಯಮು16ರಗನಾಯಕ ರವೆ ುನೆಯಕಳಸಕಂನ್ನ ಡಿಹುವುತಂಬಲಕೋಡಿಯ17ಯಿಂತೀಮರ್ಯ್ಯಾದೆಯಂಅಚಂದ್ರಾಕ್ಶ್ಯ ತಾರಂಬರೆಂಸಲಿಸುವರುಸಲಿಸಿ18ದವರ್ಗ ಸಾಯಿರಕವಿಲೆಯಗಂಗಾದೇವಿಯಲುಸಾಯಿರಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮ . ಣದಾನಂಮಾಡಿದಫಲಯಾಮರ್ಯ್ಯಾದೆಯಂತಿಡಿಸಿದವಗ್ಳೆ ಣ್ಠ19ಸಾಂಯಿರಕವಿಲೆಯಂಬಾ'ಹ ಣರುಮಂಕೊಂದಮಹಾಶಾ . . . ಕ್ರ20ಶ್ರಕರೆ . . ರುಯಿಕಲಂ ಕಾಳಿಸಟ್ಟ ನಿಲಿಸಿದೆಸಾವಂಗಲೆ ತಾಲೂಕು

ಪ್ರಮಾಣ — 4' x 2'
1. . . . . . . . ಮೂಲಸಂಭಾಯಶಂ
2. . . . . . ಪಾಲನೀಯೋ . . . . .
3. . . . . . ಶ್ರೀ . . ವಲ್ಲಭಮಹರಾಜಾಧಿರಾಜಪರಮೇಸ್ವರ
4ವರದಮಭಟ್ಟಾರಕಸಂಸತ್ಯಾಶ್ರಯಕುಳತಿಳಕುಚಾಳುಕ್ಯಾಭರಣಾನಿ (ಮತ್ತಿ 1ಶ್ರ ಭು
5ವನಮಲ್ಲದೇವರವಿಜಯರಾಜ್ಯಮುತೆ,ರೋತೆ_ರಾಭಿವೃದಿಪ್ಪವರ್ದ್ವಮಾನಮಾಚಂದ್ರಾ)
6ರ್ಕ್ಯಾತಾರೊಬರಂಸಲು . . . . ಪಂಚಮಹಾತ
7ಶಬ್ದಮಹಾಮಣ್ಡ . . . . . . .
8ನಿಜಕುಳಕಮಳಮಾ . . . . . ಶ್ರೀಮತಿ
9ಭುವನಮ್ಲದೇವ . . . . . ಶ್ರೀಮ
10ನ್ನ ಹಾಮಣ್ಣಳೇಸ್ವರೇ . . . . .
12 . . . . . ಮಾದನಾಯಕರು ॥ ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ,
13ಮಸ್ತ ಪ್ರಸಸ್ತಿ ಸಹಿತರಪ್ಪ ಶ್ರೀಮ .. ಹಾಮಂಡಳೇಶ್ವರಮನೆಯ
14 . . . . . . . ಬಾಡದೋಳಗಾಣಾ . . ಯುಮೇಲಾಳಿಕೆಯ . ಮಾ

16ಹಾಪ್ರಭುಸಿಂಗಗಾನುಣ್ಣ ನಹಂಪಗಾವುಣ್ಣನಅಶಿಯಸಮಸ್ತ)
17ಜಿಗಳ . . . . . ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ, ಶ್ರೀಮತುಚಾಳುಕ್ಯವಿಕ್ರಮ(ಗಾ)
18ಕಾಲದ . . . . . ಶುಭಕೃತುಸಂವಸತ್ತರದಮಾಘಸು ೫ ಬಿ)
19ಹಸ್ಪತಿ . . . . . ಪಾ ತ . . ತ ರಾಯಣದಸಂಕ್ರಾನಿವಿಮಿತವಾಗಿಅಳಿ
20ಯಸ್ನಾನಾಧಿಪತಿದಿವ್ಯತಸ್ತೋಧನಜ್ಞಾನಶಕ್ತಿಪಂಡಿತರಕಾಲಂಕರ್ಜ್ಜಿಧಾ
21ರಾಭೂವ್ವ್ವ೯ಕಂಮಾಡಿಕೊ)ಮಲ್ಲಿಕಾರ್ಜ್ಜುನದೇವರನಿವೇದ್ಯಕ್ಕಂಪೂಜ

text.text_original: ಅದೇ ಹೋಬಳಿ ಕಾಗೆಲೀ ಗ್ರಾಮದ ಮಲ್ಲಿಕಾರ್ಜುನ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನದ ಪ್ರಾಕಾರದಲ್ಲಿ ನೆಟ್ಟಕಲ್ಲುಪ್ರಮಾಣ — 4' x 2'1. . . . . . . . ಮೂಲಸಂಭಾಯಶಂ2. . . . . . ಪಾಲನೀಯೋ . . . . .3. . . . . . ಶ್ರೀ . . ವಲ್ಲಭಮಹರಾಜಾಧಿರಾಜಪರಮೇಸ್ವರ4ವರದಮಭಟ್ಟಾರಕಸಂಸತ್ಯಾಶ್ರಯಕುಳತಿಳಕುಚಾಳುಕ್ಯಾಭರಣಾನಿ (ಮತ್ತಿ 1ಶ್ರ ಭು5ವನಮಲ್ಲದೇವರವಿಜಯರಾಜ್ಯಮುತೆ,ರೋತೆ_ರಾಭಿವೃದಿಪ್ಪವರ್ದ್ವಮಾನಮಾಚಂದ್ರಾ)6ರ್ಕ್ಯಾತಾರೊಬರಂಸಲು . . . . ಪಂಚಮಹಾತ7ಶಬ್ದಮಹಾಮಣ್ಡ . . . . . . .8ನಿಜಕುಳಕಮಳಮಾ . . . . . ಶ್ರೀಮತಿ9ಭುವನಮ್ಲದೇವ . . . . . ಶ್ರೀಮ10ನ್ನ ಹಾಮಣ್ಣಳೇಸ್ವರೇ . . . . .12 . . . . . ಮಾದನಾಯಕರು ॥ ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ,13ಮಸ್ತ ಪ್ರಸಸ್ತಿ ಸಹಿತರಪ್ಪ ಶ್ರೀಮ .. ಹಾಮಂಡಳೇಶ್ವರಮನೆಯ14 . . . . . . . ಬಾಡದೋಳಗಾಣಾ . . ಯುಮೇಲಾಳಿಕೆಯ . ಮಾ15ದನಾಯಕರಾಳುತ್ತಿ . ॥ ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ, ಸಮಸ್ತಪ್ರಸಸ್ತಿ ಸಹಿತರಪ್ಪ ಶ್ರೀಮನ್ಮ16ಹಾಪ್ರಭುಸಿಂಗಗಾನುಣ್ಣ ನಹಂಪಗಾವುಣ್ಣನಅಶಿಯಸಮಸ್ತ)17ಜಿಗಳ . . . . . ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ, ಶ್ರೀಮತುಚಾಳುಕ್ಯವಿಕ್ರಮ(ಗಾ)18ಕಾಲದ . . . . . ಶುಭಕೃತುಸಂವಸತ್ತರದಮಾಘಸು ೫ ಬಿ)19ಹಸ್ಪತಿ . . . . . ಪಾ ತ . . ತ ರಾಯಣದಸಂಕ್ರಾನಿವಿಮಿತವಾಗಿಅಳಿ20ಯಸ್ನಾನಾಧಿಪತಿದಿವ್ಯತಸ್ತೋಧನಜ್ಞಾನಶಕ್ತಿಪಂಡಿತರಕಾಲಂಕರ್ಜ್ಜಿಧಾ21ರಾಭೂವ್ವ್ವ೯ಕಂಮಾಡಿಕೊ)ಮಲ್ಲಿಕಾರ್ಜ್ಜುನದೇವರನಿವೇದ್ಯಕ್ಕಂಪೂಜ22ರಿಗಂಪಿರಿಯಕೆರೆಯಕಳಗೆಬಿಟ್ಟಗದ್ದೆಮತ್ಮರೊಂದು ೧ ಬೆರ್ದ್ದಲೆನೂ23ರಿಂಮೂಡಕಂದಗಲೆಯದಾರಿಯಿಂಬಡಗಲುಮತ್ತಲೆರಡುಇನ್ಸ್ವೀಧರ್ಮ್ಮ24ಮವನಾವನೊರ್ರ್ಮಂಪ್ರತಿಶಾಳಿಸಿದಾತಂಪಾರಣಾಸಿಕುರುಕ್ಷೇತ)25ಪ್ರಯಾಗೆಗಂಗಾನದಿಯಲುಸಾಸಿರಕವಲೆಯಕೋಡುಂಕೊಳಗುಮಂಪೂ26ಲುಕಟ್ಟಿ[ಸಿಸಾಸಿರವೇದನಾರಗರಷ್ಟೆ ಪ್ರಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣರಕಾಲಂಕರ್ಜ್ಜಿಧಾರಾ 87 ಪೂರ್ವ ಕಂಪಾಡಿಕೊಟ್ಟ[ೈಫಲಮಕ್ಕ್ಯಾ ॥ ಅಧರ್ಮ್ಮಮನಾವನೊಮ್ಪೆನಳಿದಾತಂಅ27ಸೌಶ್ರೀತ್ರ ೯೦ಗಳಲುಅಬ್ರಾ)ಹ್ಮಣರುಮಂಅಕವಿಲೆಗಳುಮಂತನ್ನಸ್ನೆಹಸ್ತದಿಂದಂ28ವಧಿಯಿಸಿದವೊ ಮಹಾಪತಕನಕ್ಕು ! ಸ್ವದತ್ತಂಪರದ29ತ್ತ ೦ವಾಹರೇತಮಿವಸುಂಧರಾಸಷ್ಠಿ ವರುಷಸಹಸ್ರಾಣಿವಿಂವುಟ್ಟದಾವಣಗೆರೆ ತಾಲೂಕು 187Footnote1. ಯಾಂಬಾಯತೇಕಿಮಿ | ನವಿಷಂವಿಸಮಿತ್ಯಾಹುದೇವಕ್ಟಂನಿ2. ಸಮುಷ್ಯತೇವಿಷವಿಸಾಕಾಕಿನಂಹಂತಿದೇಸ್ವುಂಘುತ್ರಸೌತ್ರಿ ತ

32ದಲಿಸಾಸಿರಕವಿಲೆಯಂಸಹಾಸಿರಬ್ರಾ)ಹ್ಮಣರಿಗೆಕೊಟ್ಕ ಕೈಪಳಮಕ್ಕುಂಈ

ಅದೇ ಹೋಬಳ ಲೊಕ್ಕಿಕೆರೆ ಗ್ರಾಮದ ಪೂರ್ವಕ್ಕೆ ಈಶ್ವರದೇವರಸ್ಥಾನದ ರಂಗಮಂಟಪದ
ಆಗ್ನೇಯ ಕಂಭದಲ್ಲಿ
ಪಶ್ಚಿಮದಿಕ್ಕು
1ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಸಮಸ್ತಭುವನಾಶ್ರಯಂ ಶ್ರೀ ಪೃಥ್ವಿ
2ವಲ್ಲಭಂ ಮಹಾರಾಜಾಧಿರಾಜ ಪರಮೇಶ್ವರ ಪರ
3ಮಭಟ್ಟಾರಕ ಕಂದ್ವಾರಾವತೀಪುರವರಾಧೀಶ್ವರಂ ಯಾ
4ದವಕುಳಾಂಬರದ್ಯುಮಣಿ ಸಮ್ಯಕ್ತ ಚೂಡಾ
5ಮಣಿಮಲೆರಾಜರಾಜಮಲಪರೊಳುಗಂಡ
6ಅಸಹಾಯಶೂರನೇಕಮಂಗವೀರಸನಿವಾರಿಸಿ
7ದ್ವಿಗಿರಿದುಗ್ಗನಮಭುಜಬಳಭೀಮ ಪ್ರತಾಪಚಕ್ರ
8ವರ್ತಿಮಗರರಾಜ್ಯನಿರ್ಮ್ಮೂಲನುಂಚೋಳರಾಜ್ಯ
9ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಟಾಚಾರನುಂಮಪ್ಪಹೊಯ್ಸಿಣಕ್ರೀಸೋವಿ
10ದೇವರುಸುಕಸಂಕಥಾವಿನೋದದಿಂರಾಜ್ಯಂಗೆವ್ಯ
11ತಿರ್ದಸಕವರ್ಷಂ ೧೫ಇದುರ್ಮ್ಮುಖಿ ಸಂವತ್ಸರದಶಾ ವಣಬ
ದಕ್ಷಿಣದಿಕ್ಕು
12ಹುಳದಮವಾಸೆ ಆದಿತ್ಯವಾರಸೂರ್ಯಗ್ರೇಹೆ
13ದಂದು ಕ್ರೀಮತುಸಮಸ್ತಸುಂಕಸಬಾಧಿಕಾರಿಗ
14ುಮಪ್ಪಮಾನತ್ರತನನಾಗಂಣಬೈತೈಯ್ಯಾನಮಗರಾಥ
15 . . . ಸಿಮಯಕಂಬರಸದಂಣ್ಮಾಯಕುರು
16ಶ್ರೀಮತುಕ್ಕೇತೇಶ್ವರದೇವರನಂದಾದಿನಿಗೆ ಗೆಅಡಕೆಲೆ
17ಸುಂಕ . . . ಗೆವಲ್ಲಿನಿಬಂಧಿಯಾಗಿಕೊಟ್ಟಗದ್ಯಾಣನಾ
18ಯುಂಅವಂಗೆಸುಂಕಾಧಿಕಾರರಾದಡಂಬವಣಿ
19ಯಅಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳುಂಲೊಕಿಯಕೆಯಸ್ತ ಳದವ
ಸೀಡವಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳುಂ
21ಸಲ್ರಿ ಕೊಡುವದು ಈಧರ್ಮಕೆ - ಡಬಂದುಬೇಡೆ೧ದಡೆಶಿ ವಾರಣಾಸಿಯಸ
22 . . ಕವಿಲೆಯಂ - ತ್ರಿಗೆಯಲುಕೊಂದದೋಸ .

text.text_original: ಅದೇ ಹೋಬಳ ಲೊಕ್ಕಿಕೆರೆ ಗ್ರಾಮದ ಪೂರ್ವಕ್ಕೆ ಈಶ್ವರದೇವರಸ್ಥಾನದ ರಂಗಮಂಟಪದಆಗ್ನೇಯ ಕಂಭದಲ್ಲಿಪಶ್ಚಿಮದಿಕ್ಕು1ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಸಮಸ್ತಭುವನಾಶ್ರಯಂ ಶ್ರೀ ಪೃಥ್ವಿ2ವಲ್ಲಭಂ ಮಹಾರಾಜಾಧಿರಾಜ ಪರಮೇಶ್ವರ ಪರ3ಮಭಟ್ಟಾರಕ ಕಂದ್ವಾರಾವತೀಪುರವರಾಧೀಶ್ವರಂ ಯಾ4ದವಕುಳಾಂಬರದ್ಯುಮಣಿ ಸಮ್ಯಕ್ತ ಚೂಡಾ5ಮಣಿಮಲೆರಾಜರಾಜಮಲಪರೊಳುಗಂಡ6ಅಸಹಾಯಶೂರನೇಕಮಂಗವೀರಸನಿವಾರಿಸಿ7ದ್ವಿಗಿರಿದುಗ್ಗನಮಭುಜಬಳಭೀಮ ಪ್ರತಾಪಚಕ್ರ8ವರ್ತಿಮಗರರಾಜ್ಯನಿರ್ಮ್ಮೂಲನುಂಚೋಳರಾಜ್ಯ9ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಟಾಚಾರನುಂಮಪ್ಪಹೊಯ್ಸಿಣಕ್ರೀಸೋವಿ10ದೇವರುಸುಕಸಂಕಥಾವಿನೋದದಿಂರಾಜ್ಯಂಗೆವ್ಯ11ತಿರ್ದಸಕವರ್ಷಂ ೧೫ಇದುರ್ಮ್ಮುಖಿ ಸಂವತ್ಸರದಶಾ ವಣಬದಕ್ಷಿಣದಿಕ್ಕು12ಹುಳದಮವಾಸೆ ಆದಿತ್ಯವಾರಸೂರ್ಯಗ್ರೇಹೆ13ದಂದು ಕ್ರೀಮತುಸಮಸ್ತಸುಂಕಸಬಾಧಿಕಾರಿಗ14ುಮಪ್ಪಮಾನತ್ರತನನಾಗಂಣಬೈತೈಯ್ಯಾನಮಗರಾಥ15 . . . ಸಿಮಯಕಂಬರಸದಂಣ್ಮಾಯಕುರು16ಶ್ರೀಮತುಕ್ಕೇತೇಶ್ವರದೇವರನಂದಾದಿನಿಗೆ ಗೆಅಡಕೆಲೆ17ಸುಂಕ . . . ಗೆವಲ್ಲಿನಿಬಂಧಿಯಾಗಿಕೊಟ್ಟಗದ್ಯಾಣನಾ18ಯುಂಅವಂಗೆಸುಂಕಾಧಿಕಾರರಾದಡಂಬವಣಿ19ಯಅಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳುಂಲೊಕಿಯಕೆಯಸ್ತ ಳದವಸೀಡವಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳುಂ21ಸಲ್ರಿ ಕೊಡುವದು ಈಧರ್ಮಕೆ - ಡಬಂದುಬೇಡೆ೧ದಡೆಶಿ ವಾರಣಾಸಿಯಸ22 . . ಕವಿಲೆಯಂ - ತ್ರಿಗೆಯಲುಕೊಂದದೋಸ .

svasti samasta-bhuvanāśraya śrī-pṛthvī-vallabha mahārājādhirāja paramēśvara parama-bhaṭṭārakam
Satyāśraya-kula-tilakam Chālukyābharaṇam śrīmat-Trailōkyamalla-Dēvara rājyābhivṛddhi-pra-
varddhamānam uttarōttaram ā-chandrārkka-tāram-baram saluttam ire tat-pāda-padmōpajīvi samadhi-
gata-pañcha-mahā-śabda mahā-maṇḍalēśvaram Kuvaḷāla-pura-varēśvaram Nandagiri-nātham mada-
gajēndra-lāñchhanam Padmāvati-labdha-vara-prasādam Gaṅga-Kusumāyudham Nanniya-Gauṅgam
jayad-uttaraṅgam maṇḍalika-mukuṭa-chūḍāmaṇi maṇḍalika-lalāṭa-paṭṭam nāmādi-samasta-praśasti-
sahita śrīmat-Trailōkyamalla-Chālukya-Gaṅga-Permmanaḍi-Vikramāditya-Dēvaru Gaṅgavādi-tom-
bhattu-sāsiramum sukha-saṅkatha-vinōdadim rājyam geyyuttam ire Saka-varsha 981 neya
Vikāri-samvatsaradā Māgha-māsada puṇṇame-Ādityavārad andu Kadambaḷige-sāsirada baḷiy-agra-
hāram Bāḍada śrī-Nārāyaṇa-dēvargge nivēdyakke illiya.. lada Ēchika[v]beya magam Chittaṇḍam Piriya-
Kēta .. yakaru gauēriya ayguḷav edeya biṭṭa geḷdeya kamma 235 matta dēvargge nandā-divige naḍe-

cells.text_original:
ಅದೇ ಸ್ಥಳದಲ್ಲಿ ೨ ನೇ ಕಲ್ಲು
ಪ್ರಮಾಣ — 3' × 1' 9"
1ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಸಮಸ್ತ ಭುವನಾಶ್ರಯಶ್ರೀಪ್ರಿಥ್ವೀ ವಲ್ಲಭಮಹಾ
2ರಾಜಾಧಿರಾಜನರಮೇಶ್ವರಪರಮಭಟ್ಟಾರಕಂ ಸತ್ಯಾಶ್ರಯ
3ಕುಳತಿಳಕಂಚಾಳುಕ್ಯಾಭರಣಂಕಮತೇಳೋಕ್ಯಮಲ್ಲ
4ದೇವರರಾಜ್ಯಾಭಿ ವೃದ್ಧಿಪ್ರವರ್ದ್ವ್ಯಮಾನಮುತ್ತ ರೋತ್ಕರಮಾಚಂದ್ರಾರ್ಕ್ವತಾರಂ
5ಬರಂಸಲುತ್ತಮಿರೆತತ್ಪಾದಪದ್ಮೋಪಜೀವಿಸಮಧಿಗತಪಣ್ಣು
6ಮಣಾಳಬ್ಬಮಹಾ ಮಣ್ಣಳೇಶ್ವರಕುವಳಾಳಪುರವರೇಶ್ಚರಂನನ್ಹ
7ಗಿರಿನಾಥಂಮದಗಜೀನ್ಸ _ ಲಾಂಚ್ಚೆನಂಪದ್ಮಾ ವತೀಲಬ್ಧವರಪ್ರಸಾದಂಗಂಗ
8ಕುಸುಮಾಯುಧಂನನ್ನಿಯಗಂಗಜಯದುತ್ತ ರಂಗಂಮಣ್ಣಳಿಕವು
9ಕುಟಭೂಷಣಂಮಣ್ಣಳಿಕಲಲಾಟಪಟ್ಟಿ ಸಂಧಾಮಾದಿಸಮಸ್ತಪ್ರಸ
10ಸ್ಸಿ ಸಹಿತಶ್ರಮತೆ ಬ ಲೋಕ್ಯಮಲ್ಲಚಾಳುಕ್ಯುಗಂಗಸೆರ್ಮ್ಮನಡಿವಿಕ್ರಮಾದಿತ್ಯದೇವರು
11ಗಂಗವಾಡಿತೊಂಭತ್ತುಸಾಸಿರಮುಮಂ ಕುಕಸಂಕತಾವಿನೋದದಿಂರಾಜ್ಯಂಗೆಯ್ಯುತ್ತು
12ಮಿರ್ಕೆಸಕವರ್ಸ ೯೯೧ ನೆಯವಿಕಾರಿಸಂವತ್ಸರದನಾಘಮಾಸದಪುಣ್ಣ ಮೆ
13ಆದಿತ್ಯವಾರದನ್ಹುಕದಂಬಳಿಗೆಸಾಸಿರದಬಳಿಯಗ್ರಹಾರಂಬಾಡದಕಿಫೀ ನಾರಾಯ
14ಇದ್ದೇವರ್ಗ್ಗೆನಿವೇದ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ಇಲ್ಲಿಯಸೀಲದಐಚಿಕಬ್ಬೈಯಮಗಂಚಿತ್ರ್ಯಣ್ಣಂಪಿರಿಯಕೇಶ .
15ಯಕರುಗಣೇರಿಯಅಯ್ಸುಳವೆಡೆಯಬಿಟ್ಟಗೆ ಖಯಕಮ್ಮ ೦೩ ಮತ್ತದೇವರ್ಗ್ಗೆನ
16ನ್ಹಾದೀವಿಗೆ ನಡೆವಂತಾಗೆತಿಂಗಳ್ಳೆ ಪೊಂನಹಾಗವಟ್ಟಿ [ಯೊಳೊರ್ಸ್ಸೆಕಳುಂಸೊಟ್ಟಿಗದ್ಯಾಣ ನಾಲ್ಕು
17ಈಧಮ್ಮವೆಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪಾಲಿಸಿದವರ್‌ವಾರಣಾಸಿಯೊಳ್‌ಕುಕುಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದೊಳ್‌ಸಾಸಿರ
18ಕವಿಲೆಯಂಪೇದವಾರಗಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣರ್ಗ್ಗಂನೈಷ್ಟಿಕತಪೋಧನರ್ಗ್ಗಂಸೂರ್ಯಗೃಹ
19ದೊಲ್‌ದಾನಂಗೊಟ್ಟಫಲಮಕ್ಕುಂ ಈಧರ್ಮವನಾವನಾಮಮಳಿದಾತಂವಾರಣಾಸಿಕು
20ರುಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದೊಳ್‌ಸಾಸಿರಕವಿಲೆಯನಳಿದಪಂಚಮಹಾಪಾತಕವಕ್ಕು
21ಸ್ವದತ್ತಂಪರೆದತ್ತೆ ೦ವಾಯೋಹರೇತಿವಳುಂಧಥರಾಹಸಿ ಸರ್ವಾರ್ಷ ಸಹನಾ |
22ಹಿನಿಷ್ಕ್ಯಾಯಾಂಜಾಯತೇಕಿ)ಮಿ |

text.text_original: 1ಓಂನಮಸಿವಾಯನಮ ಸು ಂಗತಿರಶ್ನು ೦ಬಿಚಂದೆ ವ್ರ)2ಚಾಮರಚಾರವೇತೆ) ಕಳೋಕ್ಯನಗರಾರಂಭಮೂಲಸ್ತ,ಂ1 ಭಾಯಸಂಭವೇ ॥2 ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿಶ್ರೀಸಮಧಿಗತಪಂಚಮಹಾಸಬ್ದ ದ್ಧಾರಾವತೀಪುರ3 ವರಾಧೀಶ್ವರಂವಿಷ್ಟು ವಂಕೋದ್ಗವಸುವರ್ಣಗರುಡಧ್ವಜ4 ಯಾದವಕುಳಕಮಳಕಳಿಕಾವಿಕಾಸಭಾಸ್ಮರಂವಾಳವೆಯಮ5 ಲಾಯಪಿತರಾಯಪುರಸಲ್ಲಗೂಜ್ಜರರಾಯವಾರಣಾಂಕು6 ಸಂತೆಲುಂಗರಾಯಸಿರಕಮಳವಾಳೋತ್ಪಾಟನಕರಪ್ರತಿಜ್ಞಾ7 ರಾಮಭುಜಬಳಭೀಮಮಲ್ಲಾಳಂಕ್ರಿತಇತ್ಯಾದಿಸಮಸ್ತರಾಜಾವಳಿ8 ವಿರಾಜಮಾನಶ್ರೀಮತ್‌ತ್ರಭುಸ್ರತಾನಚಕವರ್ತಿಶ್ರೀವೀรมಹಾದೇವನಿ9 ಜಯರಾಜ್ಯೋದಯದತತ್ಪಾದಪದ್ಮೋಪಜೀವಿತರುಂಅತಿವಿಸಮಹ10 ಯಪಪ್ರುಢರೇಖಾರೇವಂತನುಂಪರಬರಕೃತಾಂಪ್ರಮಿಂಗಿರಿದುಗನಮ11 ಲ್ಲನೂಸೆಜಿವಳಕುವರನಾರಾಯಣಮುಂನಿರ್ಮ್ಮಿಕು ಜಗದಳತುಂಸೆ12   , ಸಾಳುವನರವೀರನುಂರಾವುತರಾಯಮಂಶ್ರೀಮತುಮಲ್ಲಿನಾ13 ಥದೇವರದಿಬ್ಬತಿ ಶ್ರೀಪಾದಪದ್ಮವಾರಾಧಕರುಮಪ್ಪುಹೆಮಾ್ರಡಿದೇವರರೆ14 ಕುಮಾರವಿಶಲದೇವರ್ಸರುಬಿಟ್ಟಸೈಧರ್ಮ್ಮಸ್ನಸ್ಸಕೀಸಕವರ್ತದ ೧೧೪೦15 ಸೆಯಸಂವತ್ಸರದಚಯಿತ)ಸುದ್ಧಚತುದ್ಧಿ ಇಸೆಸೋಮವಾರದಂ16 ಸುದವನಾರೋಪಣದಸಮೇಯದಲುಸ್ಟುಸಿ ಕೀಮದನಾದಿಯ ,17 ರಿಯಗ)ಹಾರಂಅಮಜಿಸಪ್ರವಿಸ್ಟದಹಳ್ಳಿ ಹೆಂಂಮನಬೇತೂಣಿ18 ಸ*ಮೂಲಸ್ತಾನದಕಲಿದೇವರಿಗೆಅಳೇಸಮಹಾಜನಂಗಳುಅಸನ್ನಚೆ19 ವ್ರಗಾವೆಯಸಮಕ್ಷದಲುಸೋತ)ವನುಸರ್ಮ್ಮ್ಯೃನಮಕ್ಕಿಕವಾಯವಾಗಿಧಾ20 ರಾಪೂರ್ವ್ವಕಂಮಾಡಿಬಿಟ್ಟರು ॥ ಹೆಂಮನಬೇತೂಣ -* * ಸಿದ್ದಮಲ್ಲಯ21 ದಿದೇವರಿಗೆಚಬಿುತಾ )ರೋಪಣಾದಪರ್ಮ್ಮದಲುಚತ)ವನಡಸುವಂತಾ22 ಬಿಣಿಚೆಡೆಹೊಲದಲುಗವಣಿಯಕಟ್ಟೈಯಹಿಂದೆಕಲ್ಲಗವುಡದ23 :ಸಸವಾಗಿಮತ್ನರು ೧ ಮಧಾರಾಭೂರ್ಮ್ಮಕಂಮಾಡಿಬಿಟ್ಟರು ॥ ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿಕ್ರೀಮ24 ುಮಹಾಪ ಧಾನಂಕೂಚರಗ್‌ೌಲಿಂಗರಸರುಸಿದ ಹ25 ಸಿಭೂರ್ಮ್ಮದಲುಚತ್ರ)ವನಡಸುವಂತಾಗಿಹಿರಿಯಅರಕೆಯಆ * , *26 ಕಯ್ಯಬಡಗಣಕಡೆಯಲುಮಾರಗೌಡಮುಖ್ಯವಾಗಿಮತ್ತ,ರು ೧ ಮಧಾ27 ಇರಾಪೂರ್ವ್ಮಕಂಮಾಡಿಬಿಟ್ಟರು 1 ಇಧರ್ಮ್ಮವಪ್ರತಿಬಾಲಿಸುವರು28 ತತುರ್ಮೈೇದನಇರೆಗರಷ್ಪೆ ಬ ಕಾ 999 999 699 499 99 8699 996 999
